Validation: Check the draft against the search intent: would someone who typed the keyword feel it answered them in the first screen? Mark the weakest section for the SME edit.

title: Create a content calendar
description: A multi-platform posting calendar with topics, formats, and hooks.
prompt:
Role: Act as a social media manager who plans platform-native content.

Context: Brand: [BRAND]. Platforms: [PLATFORMS]. Campaign themes / priorities for the period: [THEMES]. Audience and tone: [AUDIENCE_TONE]. Cadence per platform: [CADENCE]. Key dates / launches: [KEY_DATES]. What we are promoting: [OFFERS].

Task: Build a 2-week calendar: for each slot give the date, platform, theme, post type (e.g. carousel, short video, text), a scroll-stopping hook, the core message, a CTA, and an asset note for design. Vary formats and avoid repeating hooks.

Format: A table: Date | Platform | Theme | Format | Hook | Message | CTA | Asset note.

Verification: Flag any post that assumes an asset, offer detail or claim I did not provide. Keep each platform within its stated cadence.

Validation: Review as a member of the target audience scrolling fast: which 3 posts would actually stop them, and which feel like filler? Replace the filler.

title: Write an automated email sequence
description: Welcome, nurture, onboarding, or launch sequences with timing, subject lines, and full emails.
prompt:
Role: Act as a lifecycle marketer designing behaviour-triggered email journeys.

Context: Audience segment and lifecycle stage: [SEGMENT_STAGE]. Journey goal: [JOURNEY_GOAL]. Entry trigger: [ENTRY_TRIGGER]. Exit / success condition: [EXIT_CONDITION]. Product context: [PRODUCT_CONTEXT]. Proof assets available: [ASSETS]. Sending constraints: [CONSTRAINTS].

Task: Design a 4-6 email sequence: for each email give its single goal, the send trigger/delay, 2 subject lines, a preview text, a body outline (opening, value, one CTA), and the suppression rule. End with the metric that shows the journey is working.

Format: A table per email: Goal | Trigger/delay | Subjects | Preview | Body outline | Suppression. Then the success metric.

Verification: Every email must have exactly one CTA and one goal; flag any that drift. No invented offers or claims.

Validation: Walk the sequence as a recipient who does not convert on email 1: does each following email still make sense and add a new reason? Cut or merge any that repeat.

title: Write a campaign brief and channel plan
description: A campaign brief with objective, audience, message, channels, timeline, and measurement.
prompt:
Role: Act as a growth marketer scoping a new acquisition or activation campaign.

Context: Objective and target metric: [OBJECTIVE_METRIC]. Audience: [AUDIENCE]. Offer / hook: [OFFER]. Budget and timeframe: [BUDGET_TIME]. Channels available: [CHANNELS]. Constraints: [CONSTRAINTS]. What we learned from the last campaign: [PRIOR_LEARNINGS].

Task: Write the brief: objective, audience, single-minded proposition, key messages, mandatories, success metrics and guardrail metrics. Then a channel plan: role of each channel, rough budget split, sequencing, and one clearly-scoped experiment with a hypothesis and how you will read it.

Format: Sections: Campaign brief (headed) | Channel plan (table) | Experiment (hypothesis / setup / read). ~450 words.

Verification: Check the budget split sums to the stated budget and that every message ladders to the single proposition. Flag any channel that cannot realistically move the target metric.

Validation: Pressure-test the experiment: is it powered to give a usable read in the timeframe, or is it too small? Adjust and say what you changed.

title: Do keyword research and find content gaps
description: Keyword clusters by intent, priority topics, and the gaps competitors aren't covering.
prompt:
Role: Act as an SEO specialist doing topic and gap analysis for [SITE].

Context: Seed topics: [SEED_TOPICS]. Keyword list with volume / difficulty if available: [KEYWORD_DATA]. Existing pages that could rank: [EXISTING_PAGES]. Business priority topics: [PRIORITY_TOPICS]. Our domain strengths / weaknesses: [DOMAIN_NOTES].

Task: Group the keywords into intent-based clusters (informational / commercial / transactional / navigational). For each cluster: the head term, representative queries, the best-fit page type, whether we already have a page (map it) or it is a gap, and a priority score based on value and feasibility. List the top 5 gaps to act on first.

Format: A table: Cluster | Intent | Page type | Existing page or GAP | Priority | Note. Then the top-5 action list.

Verification: Do not invent search volumes or difficulty, only use figures I supplied, and mark clusters where data is missing. Flag any keyword whose intent is ambiguous.

Validation: Sense-check the priorities against our domain notes: are we prioritising anything we realistically cannot rank for? Re-rank if so.

title: Optimize a page for SEO
description: On-page recommendations for a URL: title, meta, headings, content gaps, internal links, and technical flags.
prompt:
Role: Act as an SEO specialist reviewing one page for on-page optimisation.

Context: URL and its purpose: [URL_PURPOSE]. Target query and intent: [TARGET_QUERY]. Current title / meta / H1: [CURRENT_TAGS]. Page content summary or paste: [CONTENT]. Known issues: [KNOWN_ISSUES]. Internal linking opportunities: [INTERNAL_LINKS].

Task: Recommend: a rewritten title tag and meta description; H1 and heading structure adjustments; content additions to fully cover the intent (as bullet gaps, not full copy); internal links to add with anchor text; and any technical flags (thin content, keyword cannibalisation, missing schema). Order everything by expected impact vs effort.

Format: Sections: Rewritten tags | Headings | Content gaps | Internal links | Technical flags | Prioritised list. ~400 words.

Verification: Base every recommendation on the content and query I provided; do not assume page elements you have not seen, list them as 'confirm on page' instead.

Validation: Check the rewritten title and meta against the intent and a realistic SERP: would a searcher click this over typical competitors? Tighten if not.

title: Create a brand messaging framework and voice guide
description: Core messages, proof points, and a voice and tone guide so everything sounds on-brand.
prompt:
Role: Act as a brand manager building the messaging framework and voice guide for [BRAND].

Context: What we do and for whom: [WHAT_WHO]. Target audiences: [AUDIENCES]. Category and main alternatives: [CATEGORY_ALTS]. Differentiators and proof: [DIFF_PROOF]. Brand personality attributes: [PERSONALITY]. Existing copy samples (good and bad): [COPY_SAMPLES]. Words we own / avoid: [LEXICON].

Goal: Give every writer and agency a single reference so brand copy is consistent, distinctive and true to how we actually sound.

Task: Produce: (1) a positioning statement and category frame; (2) 3-4 message pillars, each with a one-line claim, supporting points and proof; (3) audience-specific value messages; (4) a voice guide: 4-5 principles, each with a 'we sound like / we don't sound like' pair and a rewritten before/after example drawn from the samples; (5) the lexicon (use / avoid).

Constraints: Every claim must trace to a differentiator or proof point I provided, no aspirational claims we cannot support. Voice principles must be specific enough to change a sentence, not adjectives like 'friendly'. Keep the whole guide under ~900 words.

Examples: Voice principle shape: 'Plain over clever - We sound like: "Set it up in ten minutes." We don't sound like: "Onboarding has never been more frictionless."' Pillar shape: 'Claim -> 3 support points -> proof.'

Format: Sections: Positioning | Message pillars | Audience messages | Voice guide (principles + before/after) | Lexicon.

Verification: List any pillar or claim that lacks a proof point, and any voice principle that is really just an adjective.

Validation: Apply the voice guide to the 'bad' copy sample: does following it actually fix the sample? If not, sharpen the relevant principle.

title: Build a customer persona and buyer journey
description: Evidence-based personas with goals, pains, objections, and the journey to purchase.
prompt:
Role: Act as a product marketer building a buyer persona and journey map.

Context: Product: [PRODUCT]. Segment this persona represents: [SEGMENT]. Evidence I have (interviews, sales notes, data): [EVIDENCE]. Their role and goals: [ROLE_GOALS]. Where they learn and buy: [CHANNELS]. Known objections: [OBJECTIONS].

Task: Produce: a persona (role, goals, pains, success metrics, trusted sources, buying power); then a journey map across Awareness / Consideration / Decision / Onboarding with, per stage: the questions they are asking, their emotional state, objections, the content or proof that helps, and our current gap.

Format: Sections: Persona (card) | Journey map (table by stage). ~450 words.

Verification: Separate what is supported by the evidence from what is assumption; mark assumptions to validate with research.

Validation: Check the journey against a real recent deal in this segment: does it match how they actually bought? Note where reality differed.

title: Plan a product launch and go-to-market
description: Launch messaging, audiences, channels, timeline, and success metrics.
prompt:
Role: Act as a product marketer leading the go-to-market for a launch.

Context: What is launching and why now: [LAUNCH_WHAT_WHY]. Target audiences and their current alternative: [AUDIENCES_ALT]. Top 3 benefits with proof: [BENEFITS_PROOF]. Positioning vs competitors: [POSITIONING]. Launch tier / ambition: [TIER]. Date and constraints: [DATE_CONSTRAINTS]. Sales and channel context: [SALES_CONTEXT].

Goal: Give the launch team one aligned story and a clear plan so messaging, sales and channels all say the same thing on day one.

Task: Produce: (1) the launch narrative (problem, shift, our answer, why believe, call to action); (2) messaging by audience (headline, 3 talking points, one-liner); (3) an objection/FAQ set; (4) a GTM brief: channels and their role, asset checklist with owners, internal enablement needs, timeline milestones, and the success metrics (leading and lagging).

Constraints: Benefits must map to the proof I gave; flag any that do not. Keep the narrative under 250 words. No competitive claims that need Legal review without flagging them. Asset list must fit the launch tier.

Examples: Narrative shape: 'Today [problem]. That's because [old way]. [Product] changes it by [shift]. It works because [proof]. [CTA].' Message-by-audience row: 'Audience | Headline | 3 points | One-liner.'

Format: Sections: Launch narrative | Messaging by audience (table) | Objections/FAQ | GTM brief (channels / assets / enablement / timeline / metrics). ~900 words.

Verification: List every claim needing Legal, Security or benchmark verification before launch.

Validation: Test the narrative on someone outside the product team: can they retell it in two sentences? If not, simplify the shift.

title: Write ad copy variations and a testing plan
description: Ad copy for Meta, Google, LinkedIn, or TikTok with angles, variations, and what to test.
prompt:
Role: Act as a performance-minded growth marketer writing testable ad copy.

Context: Product and offer: [PRODUCT_OFFER]. Platform and format: [PLATFORM_FORMAT]. Audience: [AUDIENCE]. Core value prop: [VALUE_PROP]. Proof points: [PROOF]. Compliance / claim limits: [CLAIM_LIMITS]. Primary metric: [METRIC].

Task: Create 3 messaging angles (e.g. pain, outcome, social proof). For each angle write 3 variants within the platform's character limits: hook/headline, primary text, CTA. Then lay out a test matrix that isolates one variable at a time (angle, hook, CTA) so results are attributable, and state the sample/duration guidance to read it.

Format: Sections: Angles | Variants (table: Angle | Headline | Primary text | CTA) | Test matrix | Read guidance.

Verification: Check every variant against the claim limits and character limits; flag violations. No invented stats.

Validation: Review as the target audience: which angle feels most like it speaks to them, and is any variant basically a duplicate? Replace duplicates.

title: Write a press release and media pitch
description: A newsworthy press release plus a short pitch email for journalists.
prompt:
Role: Act as a PR and communications lead writing for trade and business media.

Context: Announcement: [ANNOUNCEMENT]. Why it matters and to whom: [SIGNIFICANCE]. Key facts (figures, dates, names, quotes approved): [KEY_FACTS]. Spokesperson and title: [SPOKESPERSON]. Target outlets / journalists and their beat: [TARGETS]. Boilerplate: [BOILERPLATE]. Embargo / timing: [TIMING].

Task: Write: (1) a press release - headline, dateline, strong first paragraph (who/what/why it matters), supporting paragraphs, one approved quote, boilerplate, contact; (2) a 120-word pitch email to one named target that leads with the angle relevant to their beat.

Format: Two blocks: Press release | Pitch email. AP-style, no marketing adjectives.

Verification: Use only facts and quotes from the brief; mark anything missing as [TO CONFIRM]. Do not add claims, metrics or names not supplied.

Validation: Read the first paragraph as a busy journalist: is there a real story in the first two sentences, or is it buried? Rewrite the lead if buried.

title: Design a chatbot or AI assistant conversation flow
description: Conversation flows, intents, responses, and handoff rules for a support, sales, or booking bot.
prompt:
Role: Act as a marketing operations specialist designing a website chatbot flow.

Context: Goal of the bot: [BOT_GOAL]. Pages it runs on: [PAGES]. Qualifying criteria: [QUALIFYING_CRITERIA]. Routing options (teams, booking links, content): [ROUTES]. Tone: [TONE]. Data we may collect and consent rules: [DATA_CONSENT]. Out-of-scope topics: [OUT_OF_SCOPE].

Task: Design the flow: opening message, 3-5 qualifying questions with branch logic, the routing decision for each branch, a graceful human-handoff path, a fallback for unrecognised input, and the consent/disclosure line before any data capture.

Format: A numbered flow with branches shown as indented options; a table mapping branch -> route; the consent line verbatim.

Verification: Ensure no branch collects personal data before the consent line, and every branch ends in a route or handoff (no dead ends). Flag any question that is leading.

Validation: Walk 3 visitor types (ready-to-buy, researching, wrong-fit) through the flow: does each reach a sensible outcome fast? Shorten any path over 5 steps.

title: Analyze campaign performance and ROI
description: Turns ad, email, PR, or campaign data into results, insights, and next steps.
prompt:
Role: Act as a marketing director writing a post-campaign performance review.

Context: Campaign objective and target: [OBJECTIVE_TARGET]. Spend: [SPEND]. Results data by channel (impressions, clicks, leads, conversions, revenue/pipeline): [RESULTS_DATA]. Benchmarks / prior campaign: [BENCHMARKS]. Attribution model used: [ATTRIBUTION]. Known caveats: [CAVEATS].

Task: Produce: performance vs target overall and by channel; efficiency metrics (CPL, CPA, ROAS or pipeline-to-spend); the 3 factors that most explain the outcome; what worked and what to stop; and 3 recommendations for the next campaign with expected effect.

Format: Sections: Headline result | Channel breakdown (table) | Efficiency metrics | Drivers | Keep/stop/change | Recommendations. ~500 words.

Verification: Recompute the efficiency metrics from the raw numbers and show the formulas. State how the attribution model and caveats limit the conclusions.

Validation: Challenge the read as a sceptical CFO: is the ROI claim defensible given the attribution model, or overstated? Adjust the framing.

title: Write an inclusive job description
description: A clear, inclusive job description and success profile that attracts the right candidates.
prompt:
Role: Act as a talent acquisition specialist who writes inclusive, skills-based job ads.

Context: Role title and level: [ROLE_LEVEL]. Team and manager context: [TEAM_CONTEXT]. Must-have skills and outcomes: [MUST_HAVES]. Nice-to-haves: [NICE_TO_HAVES]. Location / working pattern: [LOCATION_PATTERN]. Salary range and benefits we can state: [COMP]. Our EVP points: [EVP].

Task: Produce: (1) a job description - purpose, outcomes for the first 6-12 months, responsibilities, essential vs desirable skills (skills and behaviours, not proxies like 'degree required' unless genuinely essential), how to apply; (2) a success profile - what good looks like at 30/60/90 days with observable measures.

Format: Sections: Job description | Success profile (30/60/90 table). Plain, concise, no jargon.

Verification: Flag gendered, ageist or culturally-coded wording and any 'requirement' that is really a proxy for background rather than ability. Do not state comp or benefits beyond what I supplied.

Validation: Review as a strong candidate from a non-traditional background: would anything here wrongly screen them out? Recommend the change.

title: Create a resume screening rubric
description: Objective screening criteria and a shortlist rationale that reduce bias.
prompt:
Role: Act as a recruiter designing a fair, structured resume-screening process.

Context: Role and success profile: [ROLE_PROFILE]. Essential criteria: [ESSENTIAL]. Desirable criteria: [DESIRABLE]. Evidence types that count for each: [EVIDENCE_TYPES]. Candidate summaries (anonymised where possible): [CANDIDATES]. Legal / policy constraints: [CONSTRAINTS].

Goal: Shortlist on job-relevant evidence only, consistently across candidates, with a record that would stand up to scrutiny.

Task: Produce: (1) a scoring rubric - each criterion, its weight, and what counts as strong / partial / no evidence; (2) a scored table for the candidates with a one-line evidence-based rationale per criterion; (3) a shortlist recommendation; (4) a list of information gaps to resolve at phone screen rather than assume.

Constraints: Score only on job-relevant evidence. Do not infer age, gender, ethnicity, health, caregiving status or 'culture fit'. Ignore employment gaps unless directly job-relevant. Apply the rubric identically to every candidate. Flag, do not guess, missing information.

Examples: Rubric row: 'Criterion: stakeholder management (weight 20%). Strong = led cross-functional programme with named outcomes; Partial = contributed to cross-team work; None = not evidenced.'

Format: Sections: Rubric (table) | Scored candidates (table) | Shortlist & rationale | Gaps for phone screen.

Verification: Re-check that no score relies on a protected characteristic or a proxy for one; list any criterion applied unevenly and correct it.

Validation: Have a sceptical HR business partner review two borderline candidates: is the rationale defensible and consistent? Adjust the rubric wording if it is ambiguous.

title: Build a structured interview guide and scorecard
description: Competency-based questions, scoring anchors, and a consistent scorecard.
prompt:
Role: Act as a recruiter building a structured, competency-based interview.

Context: Role and success profile: [ROLE_PROFILE]. Competencies to assess: [COMPETENCIES]. Interview length and panel: [FORMAT_PANEL]. Level: [LEVEL]. Things to probe carefully: [PROBE_AREAS].

Task: For each competency: 2 primary behavioural questions (past behaviour, not hypotheticals), 3 follow-up probes, and a 1-4 rating scale with a concrete behavioural anchor for each level. Add an opening script, a candidate-questions slot, and a scoring summary sheet.

Format: Sections: Opening script | Per-competency (questions / probes / anchored scale) | Wrap-up | Scoring summary.

Verification: Flag any question that is leading, hypothetical, or could invite protected-characteristic information; replace it.

Validation: Run one competency past a hiring manager: would two interviewers score the same answer the same way using these anchors? Tighten anchors that are vague.

title: Create a new-hire onboarding plan
description: A 30-60-90 onboarding plan and welcome pack for a new employee.
prompt:
Role: Act as an HR operations coordinator preparing a structured onboarding.

Context: Role and team: [ROLE_TEAM]. Start date and working pattern: [START_PATTERN]. Systems and access needed: [ACCESS]. Key people to meet: [PEOPLE]. Mandatory training / policies: [MANDATORY]. First project or goal: [FIRST_GOAL].

Task: Produce: a day-by-day plan for weeks 1-2 (orientation, access, people, training, first task, check-ins); a welcome-pack checklist with an owner and a 'done by' date per item; and 3 manager prompts for the week-1 and week-2 one-to-ones.

Format: Sections: Two-week schedule (table) | Welcome-pack checklist (item / owner / due) | Manager 1:1 prompts.

title: Draft an HR policy or handbook section
description: Clear, fair policy drafts for the handbook — leave, remote work, conduct, data, and more.
prompt:
Role: Act as an HR manager drafting a policy section for the employee handbook.

Context: Policy topic: [POLICY_TOPIC]. Objectives and principles: [OBJECTIVES]. Legal / regulatory context and jurisdiction: [LEGAL_CONTEXT]. What is changing from today: [CHANGES]. Systems / forms involved: [SYSTEMS]. Tone we want: [TONE].

Task: Draft the section: purpose and scope; who it applies to; the rules in plain language; the step-by-step process with roles and timeframes; exceptions and escalation; related policies; and a short FAQ. Mark anything that needs legal or works-council review.

Format: A structured policy section with numbered clauses and an FAQ. Plain English, defined terms where needed.

Verification: Do not assert legal entitlements or obligations without a [LEGAL REVIEW] flag. Flag any clause that varies by jurisdiction.

Validation: Read it as an employee with no HR knowledge: is it clear what they must do and what happens if they do not? Rewrite the least clear clause.

title: Analyze an employee engagement survey and plan actions
description: Turns survey results into themes, priorities, and an action plan.
prompt:
Role: Act as an employee experience analyst interpreting engagement survey results.

Context: Survey scope and response rate: [SCOPE_RESPONSE]. Score data by dimension and segment: [SCORE_DATA]. Verbatim comment themes (summarised): [COMMENT_THEMES]. Prior survey comparison: [PRIOR]. Known context / events: [CONTEXT]. Constraints on action: [CONSTRAINTS].

Task: Produce: the 3-4 biggest strengths and 3-4 biggest concerns with the evidence (scores + themes); where results differ meaningfully by segment; likely drivers (clearly labelled as hypotheses); a prioritised action plan (action, rationale, owner, timeframe, how we will know it worked); and what to communicate back to employees.

Format: Sections: Strengths | Concerns | Segment differences | Driver hypotheses | Action plan (table) | Comms-back. ~550 words.

Verification: Do not over-interpret small subgroups or small score movements; note where the sample is too small. Keep driver statements as hypotheses.

Validation: Test the plan against a cynical employee who has seen surveys before: does it look like real change with owners, or a list that will not move? Strengthen the weakest action.

title: Create an employee development plan
description: A personalized growth plan with goals, experiences, learning, and support.
prompt:
Role: Act as a talent development partner building an individual growth plan.

Context: Employee's current role and level: [CURRENT_ROLE]. Their stated goals / interests: [GOALS]. Strengths and development areas from recent feedback: [FEEDBACK]. Target role or direction: [TARGET]. Time and budget available: [RESOURCES]. Business needs it should also serve: [BUSINESS_NEEDS].

Task: Produce: 3-4 development goals linked to the target and business needs; for each, specific actions using a 70/20/10 mix (experience / exposure / education), a success measure, and a timeframe; the support needed from the manager; and a check-in cadence.

Format: Sections: Goals | Development actions (table: Goal | 70 | 20 | 10 | Measure | By when) | Manager support | Check-ins. ~450 words.

Verification: Flag any action that needs budget or a role change not yet confirmed. Keep goals within the stated time and budget.

Validation: Check the plan against the employee's own words: does it serve their goal, not just the organisation's? Rebalance if it reads as one-sided.

title: Prepare a performance review with calibrated feedback
description: Evidence-based review drafts and calibrated, specific feedback.
prompt:
Role: Act as an HR business partner supporting a manager to prepare a performance review.

Context: Employee role and review period: [ROLE_PERIOD]. Goals set and results: [GOALS_RESULTS]. Evidence: peer/stakeholder feedback, examples, metrics: [EVIDENCE]. Rating scale and definitions: [RATING_SCALE]. Calibration context (team distribution, norms): [CALIBRATION]. Known risks (recency bias, one big incident, etc.): [RISKS].

Goal: Produce a review that is fair, consistent with calibration, well-evidenced, and genuinely useful for the employee's development.

Task: Produce: (1) an evidence summary against each goal / competency (strengths and gaps with specific examples); (2) a proposed rating with the rationale mapped to the scale definitions and calibration; (3) a feedback script - what went well, what to develop, framed on behaviour and impact; (4) 3 development actions for next period; (5) questions the manager should ask the employee.

Constraints: Base everything on the evidence provided; do not invent examples. Guard against recency, halo/horns and single-incident bias - flag where the evidence is thin. No comments on personal characteristics or protected traits. Keep the rating consistent with the calibration context.

Examples: Feedback shape: 'In [situation] you [behaviour], which led to [impact]. To grow, in [context] try [specific change].' Rating rationale: 'Meets = consistently delivered goals X, Y with evidence A, B; did not exceed because Z.'

Format: Sections: Evidence summary | Proposed rating & rationale | Feedback script | Development actions | Questions for the employee. ~700 words.

Verification: List every claim that lacks a specific example and every place recency or a single incident may be distorting the picture.

Validation: Review as the employee: is the rating explained by the evidence, and is the feedback actionable rather than vague? Fix the part that would feel unfair.

title: Analyze team skills gaps
description: A capability matrix showing gaps between current and needed skills, and how to close them.
prompt:
Role: Act as a talent management specialist building a team capability matrix.

Context: Team and its mandate: [TEAM_MANDATE]. Critical skills the mandate needs (with target proficiency): [REQUIRED_SKILLS]. Current people and their assessed proficiency: [CURRENT_PROFICIENCY]. Upcoming demand / strategy shifts: [FUTURE_DEMAND]. Constraints (headcount, budget, time): [CONSTRAINTS].

Task: Produce: a capability matrix (skill x person, current vs target); a gap summary per skill with severity (critical / important / minor) and single-point-of-failure risks; and a recommendation per gap using build (develop) / buy (hire) / borrow (contract or partner) with rough time and cost implications.

Format: Sections: Capability matrix (table) | Gap summary | Build/buy/borrow recommendations (table). ~450 words.

Verification: Use only the proficiencies I provided; mark skills where assessment data is missing rather than estimating. Flag gaps that are assumptions about future demand.

Validation: Check the recommendations against the constraints: is the plan actually fundable and staffable this year? Re-prioritise to what is feasible.

title: Review succession and bench strength
description: Identifies successors for key roles, readiness, and development actions.
prompt:
Role: Act as an organisational development lead running a succession and bench-strength review.

Context: Critical roles in scope and why they are critical: [CRITICAL_ROLES]. Current incumbents and flight-risk / retirement horizon: [INCUMBENTS]. Candidate pool with performance and potential signals: [CANDIDATE_POOL]. Readiness definitions: [READINESS_DEFS]. Diversity of the pipeline: [PIPELINE_DIVERSITY]. Constraints: [CONSTRAINTS].

Goal: Give leadership a clear view of where succession risk is highest and a concrete plan to build bench strength over 12-24 months.

Task: Produce: (1) a risk rating per critical role (vacancy likelihood x impact x bench depth); (2) for each role, 1-3 possible successors with readiness (ready now / 1-2 years / 3+ years) and the evidence; (3) the specific development moves (stretch assignment, exposure, mentoring) to raise readiness; (4) gaps where there is no credible successor and the mitigation; (5) a note on pipeline diversity and any concentration risk.

Constraints: Base readiness on evidence provided, not tenure or seniority alone. Do not let potential ratings stand in for demonstrated capability without noting it. Flag where the pool lacks diversity rather than ignoring it. Keep individual notes factual and defensible.

Examples: Successor row: 'Name | Readiness: 1-2 yrs | Evidence: led [X], gap in [Y] | Move: rotate through [role] for 6 months.'

Format: Sections: Role risk ratings (table) | Successors & readiness (per role) | Development moves | No-successor gaps & mitigation | Pipeline diversity note. ~650 words.

Verification: List every readiness call that rests on thin evidence and every role where the plan still leaves unacceptable risk.

Validation: Challenge as a sceptical board member: if the top two critical incumbents left this quarter, does this plan actually cover it? State the residual risk honestly.

title: Analyze attrition risk and recommend retention actions
description: Finds who is likely to leave and why, and what to do about it.
prompt:
Role: Act as a people analytics specialist analysing voluntary attrition.

Context: Population and period: [POPULATION_PERIOD]. Attrition data by segment (team, tenure, level, location, manager, performance band): [ATTRITION_DATA]. Exit interview themes: [EXIT_THEMES]. Engagement / comp / workload data available: [OTHER_DATA]. Benchmark or prior year: [BENCHMARK]. Constraints on interventions: [CONSTRAINTS].

Goal: Identify where attrition is genuinely elevated and why, and recommend actions that are proportionate and fair, without profiling individuals.

Task: Produce: overall vs benchmark; segments where attrition is meaningfully elevated (with the numbers and whether the sample supports the conclusion); likely drivers triangulated from exit themes and other data (labelled as hypotheses); 3-5 retention actions targeted at the biggest drivers with expected effect, owner and cost; and what further data would confirm the drivers.

Constraints: Report at segment level only; do not score or flag named individuals as flight risks. Do not infer protected characteristics. State sample-size limits for every segment claim. Interventions must be equitable across the affected group.

Examples: Hotspot shape: 'Segment: [team], tenure 12-24 months - attrition [X]% vs [Y]% overall, n=[N] (sufficient / caution). Exit themes: [themes].'

Format: Sections: Overall vs benchmark | Elevated segments (table) | Driver hypotheses | Retention actions (table) | Data to confirm. ~600 words.

Verification: Recompute the segment rates and show n for each; flag every segment where n is too small to conclude.

Validation: Pressure-test as an HR director: would acting on this be fair to everyone in the affected segment, and is the driver evidence strong enough to spend on? Note what you would confirm first.

title: Write an employee announcement or internal message
description: Clear, human internal communications — changes, news, policies, and benefits.
prompt:
Role: Act as an HR operations lead drafting an all-staff announcement.

Context: What is changing: [CHANGE]. Why, in plain terms: [RATIONALE]. Who is affected and how: [IMPACT]. Effective date and any actions required: [DATE_ACTIONS]. Where to get help / ask questions: [SUPPORT]. Tone: [TONE].

Task: Write the announcement: a clear subject line; what is changing and why in the first two sentences; who is affected and what (if anything) they need to do; the timeline; and where to go with questions. Acknowledge impact honestly without over-promising.

Format: Subject line + email under 220 words. Short paragraphs, one action list if needed.

title: Design a course or training program
description: Course outline, modules, objectives, activities, and assessments from a learning need.
prompt:
Role: Act as an instructional designer applying backward design.

Context: Learning need / performance gap: [LEARNING_NEED]. Audience and prior knowledge: [AUDIENCE]. Modality and total duration: [MODALITY_DURATION]. Constraints (tools, SME time, budget): [CONSTRAINTS]. Business outcome it should support: [BUSINESS_OUTCOME].

Task: Produce: 3-5 measurable learning objectives (observable verbs, tied to the performance gap); a module map with each module's objective, key content points, and one active learning method; an assessment plan aligned to each objective (formative and summative); and the SME inputs still needed.

Format: Sections: Objectives | Module map (table) | Assessment plan | SME inputs needed. ~450 words.

Verification: Check every objective is observable and assessable, and that each module and assessment maps to an objective (flag orphans). Fits within the stated duration.

Validation: Test against the performance gap: if a learner completed this, would they actually be able to do the thing on the job? Note the weakest link.

title: Storyboard an e-learning module
description: Screen-by-screen storyboard and script for an e-learning module.
prompt:
Role: Act as an instructional designer scripting a self-paced e-learning module.

Context: Module objective: [OBJECTIVE]. Content source / SME notes: [CONTENT]. Audience and reading level: [AUDIENCE]. Runtime target: [RUNTIME]. Authoring tool and interaction types available: [TOOL_INTERACTIONS]. Accessibility requirements: [ACCESSIBILITY]. Brand/style notes: [STYLE].

Task: Produce a storyboard: for each screen give the purpose, on-screen text (concise), narration script (conversational, matched to on-screen text), visual/media direction, and the interaction or knowledge check. Include an intro screen with the objective and a summary screen. Keep to the runtime.

Format: A screen-by-screen table: Screen # | Purpose | On-screen text | Narration | Visual | Interaction.

Verification: Flag any screen where narration just reads the on-screen text, any check not tied to the objective, and any media that would fail the accessibility requirements.

Validation: Review as a learner clicking through: is each screen doing one job, and does the module hold attention for its runtime? Cut or merge weak screens.

title: Create a quiz or test with answer key
description: Assessment items at the right difficulty, mapped to learning objectives, with answers and explanations.
prompt:
Role: Act as an instructional designer and assessment writer.

Context: Learning objectives: [OBJECTIVES]. Content covered: [CONTENT]. Audience and level: [AUDIENCE]. Item formats allowed: [FORMATS]. Number of items and coverage weighting: [BLUEPRINT]. Stakes (formative / certification): [STAKES].

Task: Produce an assessment blueprint (objective x number of items x cognitive level), then the items: for each, the stem, options (with plausible distractors based on real misconceptions), the key, a one-line rationale for the key and for why each distractor is wrong, and the objective it assesses. Aim for application-level items, not just recall.

Format: Sections: Blueprint (table) | Items (numbered, each with stem/options/key/rationale/objective).

Verification: Flag items that are ambiguous, have grammatical give-aways, test recall of trivia, or do not map to an objective. Ensure exactly one defensible key each.

Validation: Answer a sample of items as a knowledgeable learner and as a guessing one: do the strong learners pass and can the items be gamed? Fix any that can.

title: Write a facilitator guide and session run sheet
description: Everything a facilitator needs to deliver a session: timing, scripts, activities, and materials.
prompt:
Role: Act as a corporate trainer preparing to facilitate a live session.

Context: Session topic and objectives: [TOPIC_OBJECTIVES]. Audience, size and room/virtual setup: [AUDIENCE_SETUP]. Total time and any fixed breaks: [TIME]. Content and slides available: [MATERIALS]. Facilitator experience level: [FACILITATOR_LEVEL]. Known tricky moments: [TRICKY_MOMENTS].

Task: Produce a run sheet: each segment with start time, duration, objective, what the facilitator says / does (brief script), the activity and its instructions, materials needed, and transition. Add an opening and close, timing checkpoints, and a contingency plan for running long or low energy.

Format: A table: Time | Duration | Segment | Facilitator actions | Activity | Materials. Plus opening, close, and contingencies.

Verification: Check the durations sum to the available time including breaks; flag any activity whose instructions are unclear or that needs materials not listed.

Validation: Walk it as a first-time facilitator: could they run this without guessing? Add detail where they would stall.

title: Design a workshop activity or discussion
description: Engaging activities and discussions that achieve a specific learning outcome.
prompt:
Role: Act as a workshop facilitator designing a single active learning activity.

Context: Learning point the activity must land: [LEARNING_POINT]. Group size and setup: [GROUP_SETUP]. Time available: [TIME]. Materials available: [MATERIALS]. Energy level / point in the day: [CONTEXT].

Task: Design the activity: a one-line purpose, setup, step-by-step participant instructions, timing per step, the facilitator's role during it, 3-4 debrief questions that connect it to the learning point, and a lower-tech or shorter variation.

Format: Sections: Purpose | Setup | Instructions (timed steps) | Facilitator role | Debrief questions | Variation.

title: Build a personalized learning pathway
description: An adaptive learning path based on a learner's role, level, and goals.
prompt:
Role: Act as a learning experience designer building an adaptive pathway.

Context: Target role or capability: [TARGET]. Learner starting points that exist: [STARTING_POINTS]. Available content and modalities: [CONTENT_LIBRARY]. Time expectation: [TIME_EXPECTATION]. Definition of 'done' for the pathway: [COMPLETION_DEF]. Constraints: [CONSTRAINTS].

Task: Design: an entry diagnostic and how its results route learners; a core spine everyone does; branch modules by starting point or goal; checkpoints with pass criteria; on-the-job application tasks; and manager touchpoints. Show the branching logic explicitly.

Format: Sections: Diagnostic & routing | Core spine | Branches (table: condition -> modules) | Checkpoints | Application tasks | Manager touchpoints. ~500 words.

Verification: Ensure every branch condition leads somewhere and every learner reaches the completion definition. Flag branches with no content to support them.

Validation: Trace two personas (novice, experienced) through the pathway: is each path the right length and not repetitive? Adjust.

title: Define a competency framework
description: Competencies with proficiency levels and observable behaviors.
prompt:
Role: Act as a capability building lead defining a competency framework for a job family.

Context: Job family and roles it covers: [JOB_FAMILY]. Strategic capabilities the business needs from it: [STRATEGIC_CAPABILITIES]. Existing frameworks or inputs: [EXISTING_INPUTS]. Number of proficiency levels wanted: [LEVELS]. How it will be used (hiring, development, promotion): [USE]. Constraints: [CONSTRAINTS].

Goal: Produce a framework specific enough that two managers would rate the same person similarly and that connects directly to development and progression decisions.

Task: Produce: 6-9 competencies grouped into 2-3 clusters; a one-paragraph definition per competency (observable, not abstract); behavioural anchors at each proficiency level (what a person at that level actually does, with an example); the anchors that typically distinguish adjacent levels; and guidance on evidence sources for assessment.

Constraints: Anchors must describe observable behaviour and outputs, not traits or attitudes. Adjacent levels must be genuinely distinguishable, not just 'more' of the same adjective. Keep the whole framework usable in under ~1200 words. Align verbs to how it will be used.

Examples: Anchor shape: 'Level 3 - Independently leads [X] across teams; anticipates [risk] and adjusts; e.g. redesigned [process] reducing [metric].' Level distinction: 'L2->L3 = shifts from executing within a team to coordinating across teams.'

Format: Sections: Cluster & competency list | Per-competency (definition + level anchors + level distinctions) | Assessment evidence guidance.

Verification: Flag any anchor that is a trait not a behaviour, and any adjacent pair that a rater could not tell apart.

Validation: Apply the framework to one real person you describe: can you place them at a level with evidence, and does the next level give a clear development target? Sharpen where it is fuzzy.

title: Run a learning needs analysis
description: Identifies what a role or team needs to learn — and what isn't a training problem.
prompt:
Role: Act as a capability building lead conducting a learning needs analysis.

Context: Team or role in scope: [SCOPE]. Business goal and the performance it depends on: [GOAL_PERFORMANCE]. Evidence of the current gap (metrics, manager input, observations): [EVIDENCE]. What has been tried: [PRIOR]. Constraints: [CONSTRAINTS].

Task: Produce: the specific performance gaps (current vs required, with evidence); a root-cause read for each (skill / knowledge / motivation / environment / process) - be explicit that not all gaps are training problems; recommended interventions split into learning and non-learning (process, tools, incentives, management); and a prioritised plan by impact and feasibility.

Format: Sections: Performance gaps | Root causes | Interventions (learning / non-learning) | Priorities (table). ~450 words.

Verification: Flag every gap where the evidence is thin, and every case where training is unlikely to fix the real cause.

Validation: Challenge as a sceptical business sponsor: which recommended item would actually change the metric, and which is training for its own sake? Cut the latter.

title: Design an internal knowledge assistant
description: How an AI assistant should answer employee questions from your documents: sources, tone, and escalation.
prompt:
Role: Act as a capability building lead preparing content for an internal knowledge assistant.

Context: Topic domain: [DOMAIN]. Source material: [SOURCE_MATERIAL]. Audience and their common tasks: [AUDIENCE_TASKS]. Questions people actually ask: [REAL_QUESTIONS]. What must be kept current / owned: [OWNERSHIP]. Out-of-scope or sensitive areas: [OUT_OF_SCOPE].

Task: Produce: 8-12 atomic articles (one question or task each) with a clear title, a direct answer first, steps or detail, and 'related' links; a matching FAQ list phrased in users' words; metadata per article (owner, last-reviewed, review cadence); and rules for questions the assistant should route to a human.

Format: Sections: Articles (each: title / answer / detail / related) | FAQ list | Metadata table | Human-routing rules.

Verification: Each article must answer exactly one question and cite the source material; flag anything not supported by the sources or that touches an out-of-scope area.

Validation: Test with 3 of the real questions: does the assistant content answer them directly without the user reading a whole policy? Tighten any that bury the answer.

title: Write a role-play or scenario simulation for training
description: Realistic practice scenarios with roles, branches, and debrief questions.
prompt:
Role: Act as a corporate trainer designing a scenario-based role-play.

Context: Skill being practised: [SKILL]. Realistic context / setting: [SETTING]. Roles involved: [ROLES]. Learner level: [LEVEL]. Time available: [TIME]. Common mistakes learners make: [COMMON_MISTAKES]. Observation criteria: [OBSERVATION_CRITERIA].

Task: Produce: a scenario brief; a role card for each role (goal, information they hold, constraints); 2-3 decision points, each with options and realistic consequences that branch the scenario; an observer checklist tied to the criteria; and a debrief guide (what happened / why / what to do differently).

Format: Sections: Brief | Role cards | Decision points (option -> consequence) | Observer checklist | Debrief guide.

Verification: Ensure each role card only reveals what that role would know, and each decision point has a genuinely different consequence per option. Flag any that railroads to one outcome.

Validation: Play it through making the common mistakes: does the scenario surface them and does the debrief address them well? Adjust the weak decision point.

title: Build a business budget with driver assumptions
description: An annual or project budget built from clear drivers and assumptions.
prompt:
Role: Act as an FP&A analyst building a driver-based annual budget.

Context: Entity / cost centre: [ENTITY]. Prior-year actuals and current run-rate: [PRIOR_ACTUALS]. Business plan inputs (volume, headcount, pricing, initiatives): [PLAN_INPUTS]. Known cost drivers and their rates: [COST_DRIVERS]. Constraints / targets from leadership: [TARGETS]. Chart of accounts structure: [COA].

Task: Produce: the driver tree linking business inputs to P&L lines; an assumptions log (each assumption, its value, source, and owner); the build sequence (which lines to model first and dependencies); the key sensitivities to test; and the review checkpoints before submission.

Format: Sections: Driver tree | Assumptions log (table) | Build sequence | Sensitivities | Review checkpoints. ~450 words.

Verification: Flag every assumption without a named source or owner, and any P&L line not connected to a driver. Do not invent rates - mark [INPUT NEEDED].

Validation: Sanity-check the implied totals against prior-year run-rate: are the growth/cost movements explainable by the plan inputs? Flag any line that jumps without a reason.

title: Explain budget vs. actual variances
description: Analyzes variances and writes the commentary management needs.
prompt:
Role: Act as an FP&A analyst writing the monthly variance commentary.

Context: Period and entity: [PERIOD_ENTITY]. Actuals vs budget by line (and vs prior year / forecast): [VARIANCE_DATA]. Materiality threshold for commentary: [MATERIALITY]. Known one-offs and timing items: [ONE_OFFS]. Business context / events: [CONTEXT].

Task: Produce: a variance summary (favourable / adverse, permanent vs timing); for each material line, the driver-level explanation (price / volume / mix / rate / phasing / one-off) with the numbers; the net read for the period; and the implication for the full-year outlook per line.

Format: Sections: Summary | Line-by-line (table: Line | Variance | Driver split | Permanent/Timing | FY implication) | Net read. ~450 words.

Verification: Ensure the driver splits reconcile to each line's total variance; separate timing from permanent clearly; flag lines where the cause is unknown rather than guessing.

Validation: Read as a business partner who will face the budget holder: is each explanation specific enough to act on, or hand-wavy? Sharpen the vaguest one.

title: Forecast cash flow and review working capital
description: A cash flow forecast, runway, and working-capital levers.
prompt:
Role: Act as a finance business partner producing a 13-week cash flow forecast and working-capital review.

Context: Opening cash and facilities: [OPENING_CASH]. Receivables ageing and collection pattern: [AR_DATA]. Payables terms and payment run schedule: [AP_DATA]. Inventory position if relevant: [INVENTORY]. Known large in/outflows and their timing: [KNOWN_FLOWS]. Revenue / billing schedule: [BILLING]. Covenants or minimum-cash requirements: [COVENANTS].

Goal: Give the business a reliable view of the cash position over 13 weeks, the tightest points, and the actions that most improve it.

Task: Produce: (1) a 13-week cash forecast (opening, receipts, payments, closing) with the assumptions per major line; (2) the weeks where cash falls below the comfort / covenant level and by how much; (3) a working-capital diagnosis - DSO, DPO, DIO vs target and the cash tied up in each; (4) prioritised levers (collections focus, terms, payment timing, inventory) with the estimated cash release and any commercial trade-off; (5) what to monitor weekly.

Constraints: Do not assume collections faster than the stated pattern without flagging it as a target. Payment timing changes must respect supplier terms - flag any that do not. Keep every figure traceable to the inputs. Note covenant implications explicitly.

Examples: Lever row: 'Tighten collections on top-10 overdue accounts -> ~[value] within 3 weeks; trade-off: relationship risk on [account].' Tight-week flag: 'Week 6 closing cash [value] vs covenant minimum [value] -> shortfall [value].'

Format: Sections: 13-week forecast (table) | Tight weeks | Working-capital diagnosis | Levers (table) | Weekly monitoring list. ~650 words.

Verification: Recompute closing cash week to week and the DSO/DPO/DIO figures; show the method. Flag assumptions that differ from the stated patterns.

Validation: Pressure-test as a treasurer: if receipts run one week late across the board, does the business still clear its covenant? State the residual risk and the earliest warning sign.

title: Analyze financial statements
description: Reads a P&L, balance sheet, and cash flow statement and summarizes performance, health, and risks.
prompt:
Role: Act as a financial controller analysing a company's financial statements.

Context: Statements provided (P&L, balance sheet, cash flow) and periods: [STATEMENTS_PERIODS]. Sector and any peer/benchmark data: [SECTOR_BENCHMARK]. Known events affecting comparability: [EVENTS]. Audience and their question: [AUDIENCE_QUESTION]. Accounting-policy notes that matter: [POLICY_NOTES].

Goal: Explain what the numbers actually say about performance and financial health, and what deserves management attention.

Task: Produce: (1) trend and common-size analysis of the P&L; (2) key ratios across profitability, liquidity, working-capital efficiency and leverage, each with the calculation, the trend, and a plain reading; (3) the quality-of-earnings and cash-conversion picture; (4) 3-5 findings that need management attention; (5) an executive summary (~150 words) answering the audience's question.

Constraints: Use only the figures in the statements; show every ratio formula. Adjust for the comparability events and say how. Do not opine beyond what the statements support - flag where you would need more data (e.g. segment detail).

Examples: Ratio line: 'Gross margin: 61% -> 58% -> 55% over three periods; driven by [X per notes]; below the [sector] benchmark of ~60%.'

Format: Sections: P&L trend & common-size | Ratio analysis (table) | Earnings quality & cash conversion | Findings for management | Executive summary. ~700 words.

Verification: Recompute a sample of the ratios and reconcile net income to operating cash flow; list any figure that does not tie.

Validation: Review as an audit partner: is any conclusion stronger than the statements justify? Soften or evidence it, and name what disclosure would settle the open questions.

title: Find cost savings and improve profitability
description: Cost and profitability analysis with practical, prioritized savings options.
prompt:
Role: Act as a management accountant analysing product / customer / channel profitability.

Context: Dimension to analyse (product / customer / channel / region): [DIMENSION]. Revenue and cost data by that dimension, including cost allocation basis: [DATA]. Fixed vs variable cost split: [COST_SPLIT]. Strategic priorities / constraints (e.g. cannot exit a segment): [CONSTRAINTS]. Target margin or savings: [TARGET].

Task: Produce: a contribution and full-cost margin view by segment; the cost drivers explaining the low-margin segments; the effect of the allocation basis on the picture (and a sensitivity to a different basis); and prioritised optimisation options (price, mix, cost-to-serve, process, exit) with estimated margin impact and the commercial risk of each.

Format: Sections: Margin by segment (table) | Cost-driver analysis | Allocation sensitivity | Optimisation options (table: Option | Margin impact | Risk). ~500 words.

Verification: State the allocation assumptions and show how the ranking changes under the alternative basis. Flag segments where cost data is estimated.

Validation: Challenge as a commercial leader: which option is actually executable next quarter without breaking a customer relationship or the constraints? Re-rank to reality.

title: Investigate reconciliation exceptions
description: Works through unmatched items in bank or ledger reconciliations.
prompt:
Role: Act as an accountant reviewing bank reconciliation exceptions.

Context: Reconciliation period and account: [PERIOD_ACCOUNT]. Unreconciled items (date, amount, description, GL side vs bank side): [EXCEPTIONS]. Common recurring causes in this account: [COMMON_CAUSES]. Cut-off date: [CUTOFF].

Task: For each exception: classify it (timing / missing entry / duplicate / error / bank charge / unidentified), state the most likely cause, the next action (who does what), and whether it is a cut-off item. Then summarise by category and flag anything that looks unusual or above a materiality line for escalation.

Format: A table: Item | Amount | Category | Likely cause | Next action | Cut-off? Plus a category summary and escalation flags.

title: Plan an audit or internal control review
description: Audit scope, risks, controls to test, PBC list, and working-paper checklist.
prompt:
Role: Act as an internal auditor planning fieldwork for a specific area.

Context: Area / process in scope: [AREA]. Objectives of the audit: [OBJECTIVES]. Known risks and prior findings: [KNOWN_RISKS]. Key controls as described by management: [CONTROLS]. Data and systems available: [DATA_SYSTEMS]. Period and materiality: [PERIOD_MATERIALITY]. Standards / methodology to follow: [METHODOLOGY].

Goal: Produce a plan that focuses effort on the highest risks, with procedures that would actually detect a material problem, and a clean list of what to request from the business.

Task: Produce: (1) a risk assessment for the area (risk, likelihood, impact, linked assertion or objective); (2) for each significant risk, the control(s) relied on and the test of design and operating effectiveness; (3) substantive procedures where controls are weak, including a sampling approach (population, method, size rationale); (4) the data analytics to run; (5) a prepared-by-client (PBC) request list with owners and dates.

Constraints: Every procedure must trace to a stated risk or objective - no procedures 'because we always do them'. Sample sizes must have a stated rationale. Do not assume controls operate as described - the plan is to test that. Follow the given methodology.

Examples: Procedure row: 'Risk: unauthorised vendor changes. Control: dual approval. Test of operating effectiveness: reperform approval on a sample of [N] changes across the period; substantive: match [N] payments to approved vendor master.'

Format: Sections: Risk assessment (table) | Controls & tests | Substantive procedures & sampling | Data analytics | PBC list (table). ~700 words.

Verification: Check that every significant risk has at least one procedure and every procedure maps back to a risk; flag any sample size without a rationale.

Validation: Challenge as an audit manager: if the key control were failing all year, would this plan catch it? Strengthen the procedure that would not.

title: Review transactions for anomalies and fraud indicators
description: Flags suspicious patterns in transactions and how to investigate them.
prompt:
Role: Act as an auditor performing an analytical review of transactions for anomalies and fraud indicators.

Context: Dataset and fields (e.g. vendor payments, expenses, journals): [DATASET_FIELDS]. Period and volume: [PERIOD_VOLUME]. Known control environment and approval limits: [CONTROLS_LIMITS]. Red-flag indicators to test (e.g. round amounts, just-below-approval, duplicate, weekend postings, new vendor + fast payment, split transactions): [INDICATORS]. Materiality / focus: [FOCUS].

Goal: Surface the transactions most worth a closer look, with a clear reason, without accusing anyone on the basis of a pattern alone.

Task: Produce: (1) the test logic for each indicator (how you would define and detect it in this dataset); (2) a ranked findings list - transaction reference, indicator(s) triggered, why it is notable, risk rating, and whether a single innocent explanation is likely; (3) grouped patterns (same vendor / user / period); (4) the specific documents and steps to investigate each top finding; (5) what a clean explanation would look like for each.

Constraints: An anomaly is a question, not a conclusion - never state or imply that a named person committed fraud. Every finding needs a factual basis in the data. Note where the indicator commonly has benign causes. Keep individual references factual.

Examples: Finding row: 'Ref [X] | Indicators: amount 4,950 just below 5,000 limit + vendor added 2 days prior | Risk: high | Benign explanation possible: yes (genuine small purchase) | Investigate: PO, quote, vendor due-diligence file, approver.'

Format: Sections: Indicator test logic | Ranked findings (table) | Pattern groups | Investigation steps per top finding | Clean-explanation criteria. ~650 words.

Verification: State the assumptions behind each detection rule and the false-positive risk; flag indicators that cannot be tested with the fields available.

Validation: Review as a forensic lead: would each top finding survive as a reasonable basis to ask questions, or is it noise? Drop the noise and say why.

title: Write a month-end close report
description: The month-end narrative and management report: performance, variances, and issues.
prompt:
Role: Act as a financial controller writing the month-end management report narrative.

Context: Period and entity: [PERIOD_ENTITY]. Results vs budget and prior year (P&L summary): [RESULTS]. Balance-sheet movements of note: [BS_MOVEMENTS]. Cash position and movement: [CASH]. Accruals / estimates / one-offs booked: [ADJUSTMENTS]. Open items and risks: [OPEN_ITEMS]. Audience: [AUDIENCE].

Task: Write: a results summary vs plan and prior year; the 3-4 drivers of the variance; balance-sheet and cash commentary on material movements; the significant judgements and estimates in the period; the risks and open items with owners; and the actions being taken.

Format: Sections: Results summary | Variance drivers | Balance sheet & cash | Judgements & estimates | Risks & open items | Actions. ~500 words.

Verification: Tie every driver to a number; separate one-offs and phasing from underlying performance; flag any estimate that could still move materially.

Validation: Read as the audience seeing only this page: is it clear how the month really went and what needs their attention? Remove anything that is just description.

title: Prepare a board financial pack and talking points
description: A board-ready financial summary with key messages and anticipated questions.
prompt:
Role: Act as a CFO preparing the finance section of the board pack.

Context: Reporting period and prior guidance: [PERIOD_GUIDANCE]. Performance summary vs plan and prior year: [PERFORMANCE]. Cash, liquidity and covenant position: [CASH_COVENANTS]. Forecast / outlook and key assumptions: [OUTLOOK]. Capital allocation matters for decision: [CAPITAL]. Top financial risks: [RISKS]. Board's known concerns: [BOARD_CONCERNS].

Goal: Give the board a clear, honest read on financial performance, outlook and risk, and equip the CFO for the discussion.

Task: Produce: (1) a one-page performance summary (vs plan, vs prior year, vs guidance) with the drivers; (2) outlook and the assumptions it depends on, including range; (3) cash, liquidity and covenant headroom; (4) the financial risks with mitigation and any decision the board is asked to make; (5) 5-7 talking points; (6) the 6 hardest questions the board will ask and a crisp answer to each.

Constraints: No number without a comparison point. Present guidance variance and any covenant pressure plainly - do not soften. Assumptions behind the outlook must be explicit. Keep the written section under ~700 words plus the Q&A.

Examples: Talking point: 'Revenue is [X]% below plan; two-thirds is timing on [deals] expected to close in Q[n], one-third is [permanent cause].' Q&A: 'Q: Is the covenant at risk? A: Headroom is [X] at period end; under the downside it narrows to [Y] in [month]; mitigations are [Z].'

Format: Sections: Performance summary | Outlook & assumptions | Cash & covenants | Risks & decisions | Talking points | Anticipated Q&A.

Verification: Reconcile the performance summary to the detailed results and the outlook to the assumptions list; flag anything that does not tie.

Validation: Rehearse as a challenging non-executive director: which answer sounds evasive or over-optimistic? Rewrite it to be straight.

title: Draft a contract from a term sheet
description: A first-pass commercial contract built from agreed terms, for lawyer review.
prompt:
Role: Act as a contracts manager preparing a first-pass draft of a commercial agreement for legal review.

Context: Agreement type: [AGREEMENT_TYPE]. Parties and roles: [PARTIES]. Agreed commercial terms (term sheet): [TERM_SHEET]. Our contracting playbook positions and fallbacks: [PLAYBOOK]. Governing law and any regulatory overlay: [LAW_REGULATORY]. Deal-specific risks: [DEAL_RISKS]. Template or precedent to base it on: [PRECEDENT].

Goal: Produce a clean first draft that reflects the term sheet and our preferred positions, so legal review is about judgement calls, not fixing structure.

Task: Draft the agreement section by section from the precedent: reflect every term-sheet point; use our preferred playbook position for each key clause and note the agreed fallback in a comment; insert placeholders for anything not yet agreed; and produce (a) a list of open points needing instruction, (b) a list of clauses that must have qualified legal review before sending.

Constraints: This is a drafting aid, not legal advice. Do not state legal conclusions or opine on enforceability. Do not invent commercial terms - use [TO BE CONFIRMED]. Keep defined terms consistent. Flag any clause where the playbook is silent.

Examples: Clause note shape: 'Limitation of liability - drafted at our preferred cap ([X]); playbook fallback is [Y]; do not go below [Z] without GC approval.'

Format: A drafted agreement with numbered clauses and inline [COMMENTS], followed by: Open points | Clauses requiring legal review.

Verification: Cross-check every term-sheet item appears in the draft; list any that do not. Flag every placeholder and every deviation from the precedent.

Validation: Have a qualified lawyer review before this is sent to a counterparty - this draft must not leave the building without that review. Note the three clauses most likely to be negotiated.

title: Review a contract and flag risky clauses
description: A risk-ranked issues list, suggested redlines, and questions before you sign.
prompt:
Role: Act as legal counsel reviewing a counterparty's contract draft.

Context: Contract and its purpose: [CONTRACT_PURPOSE]. The counterparty draft (paste or summary by clause): [DRAFT]. Our playbook / acceptable positions: [PLAYBOOK]. Our risk appetite and must-nots: [RISK_APPETITE]. Deal context and leverage: [DEAL_CONTEXT]. Governing law: [LAW].

Goal: Give the deal team a clear, prioritised view of where this contract exposes us and what to push back on.

Task: Produce: (1) a risk-ranked issues list - clause reference, the issue in plain English, the business impact if unchanged, our playbook position, and a suggested redline or fallback; (2) the 3-5 points that are deal-blockers vs negotiable; (3) missing protections we would normally expect; (4) questions for the business before we respond.

Constraints: Identify issues and positions; do not give a legal opinion on enforceability or litigation outcome. Base risk ratings on our stated appetite. Do not assume facts not in the draft - flag ambiguities instead. Quote clause references, not long extracts.

Examples: Issue row: 'Cl. 11.2 Indemnity - uncapped and covers indirect loss. Impact: unlimited exposure on [scenario]. Playbook: mutual, capped at fees. Suggested: cap at 12 months' fees, carve back indirect loss.'

Format: Sections: Risk-ranked issues (table) | Deal-blockers vs negotiable | Missing protections | Questions for the business.

Verification: Check each issue cites a real clause in the draft and each rating matches the stated risk appetite; flag clauses you could not fully assess.

Validation: A qualified lawyer must confirm the positions before redlines go back. Sanity-check the top 3 issues against the deal leverage: are we pushing where we can actually win?

title: Compare clauses across contract versions
description: Side-by-side comparison of what changed between drafts and why it matters.
prompt:
Role: Act as a contracts manager comparing versions of an agreement.

Context: Document / clauses in scope: [SCOPE]. Version A (ours / prior): [VERSION_A]. Version B (counterparty / new): [VERSION_B]. Our acceptable positions: [PLAYBOOK]. What we care about most: [PRIORITIES].

Task: Produce a change table: for each substantive change, quote the before/after (short), describe the effect in plain English, say whether it moves risk toward or away from us, rate it (acceptable / negotiate / reject) against the playbook, and suggest the response. Ignore purely stylistic edits but note if a 'style' edit changes meaning.

Format: A table: Clause | Before | After | Effect | Risk direction | Verdict | Suggested response. Plus a summary of the 3 most important changes.

Verification: Flag any change where the effect is ambiguous and any 'minor' edit that actually shifts an obligation or a defined term.

Validation: Have counsel confirm the verdicts on anything rated 'negotiate' or 'reject'. Check the summary picks the changes that matter to our priorities, not just the biggest text edits.

title: Summarize a contract and its obligations in plain English
description: What you've agreed to: obligations, dates, money, and risks — for non-lawyers.
prompt:
Role: Act as a contracts manager summarising an executed contract for the operational team.

Context: Contract (paste or clause-by-clause summary): [CONTRACT]. Who needs the summary and why: [AUDIENCE_PURPOSE]. Systems where obligations/dates will be tracked: [TRACKING_SYSTEM]. Known hot spots: [HOT_SPOTS].

Task: Produce: a key-terms table (parties, effective date, term and renewal, value and payment terms, governing law); an obligations register (obligation, responsible party, trigger, deadline, consequence of breach); the notice periods and how notice must be given; the termination rights on each side; and a short risk-flags list for the business.

Format: Sections: Key terms (table) | Obligations register (table) | Notices | Termination rights | Risk flags.

Verification: Cite the clause number for every extracted item; mark anything ambiguous as 'confirm with legal' rather than interpreting.

Validation: Check the obligations register against the contract end to end: is anything with a deadline or a financial consequence missing? Add it.

title: Write a legal research memo
description: An issue–rule–analysis–conclusion memo on a legal question.
prompt:
Role: Act as legal counsel preparing an internal research memo for a colleague to verify.

Context: The legal question / scenario: [QUESTION_SCENARIO]. Jurisdiction and area of law: [JURISDICTION_AREA]. Relevant facts: [FACTS]. Sources I have provided (statutes, cases, guidance): [PROVIDED_SOURCES]. What the business wants to do: [BUSINESS_AIM]. Risk tolerance: [RISK_TOLERANCE].

Goal: Give a colleague a well-organised starting memo that frames the issue and analysis clearly and makes explicit exactly what must be checked before anyone relies on it.

Task: Produce an IRAC memo: (1) Issue - the precise legal question(s); (2) Rule - the applicable framework from the provided sources, with citations, and where the law is unsettled; (3) Application - apply the rule to the facts, both ways where arguable; (4) Conclusion - the likely position and the residual risk; (5) a 'to verify' list - every proposition that needs a source check, and the sources not yet reviewed.

Constraints: Rely only on the sources I provided; do not cite cases, sections or holdings from memory - if a source is needed and not provided, list it as a gap. Do not overstate certainty in an unsettled area. This memo is not legal advice and is not to be relied on until verified by a qualified lawyer.

Examples: Rule paragraph shape: 'Under [statute s.X] ... In [Case] the court held ... [citation, provided]. It is unsettled whether ... [gap - needs research].'

Format: Sections: Issue | Rule | Application | Conclusion & residual risk | To verify (list). ~700 words.

Verification: Mark every legal proposition as (a) supported by a provided source with a pinpoint citation, or (b) unverified. There must be no unmarked assertions of law.

Validation: A qualified lawyer must verify every citation and the analysis before this is relied on. Flag the point where the outcome is most sensitive to how the law is interpreted.

title: Summarize a case or regulation
description: Summarizes case law or regulations with holdings, reasoning, and implications.
prompt:
Role: Act as a paralegal preparing a summary note of a provided legal source.

Context: Source type and citation: [SOURCE_CITATION]. Full text or long extract provided: [SOURCE_TEXT]. Why we are looking at it / the question it might bear on: [OUR_QUESTION]. Audience: [AUDIENCE].

Task: Produce: for a case - parties, facts, procedural posture, issue(s), holding, the court's reasoning, and any dissent; for a regulation - scope, who it binds, the key obligations and dates, definitions that matter, and enforcement. Then a short 'relevance to us' note framed as questions for a lawyer, not conclusions. Keep pinpoint references to the source.

Format: Sections: Overview | Key content (holding / obligations) | Reasoning / detail | Relevance to us (as open questions). Pinpoint cites throughout.

Verification: Every statement must be traceable to a passage in the provided text - add the paragraph/section reference. Do not add context or related authority from memory.

Validation: Check the summary against the source for anything overstated or missing on the points relevant to our question. A lawyer should confirm the 'relevance' framing.

title: Assess the impact of a regulatory change
description: What a new rule requires, who it affects, and what must change.
prompt:
Role: Act as a regulatory affairs specialist assessing the impact of a regulatory change.

Context: The change (instrument, citation, effective/transition dates): [CHANGE_DETAILS]. Official text or summary provided: [CHANGE_TEXT]. Our business activities, products and jurisdictions in scope: [BUSINESS_SCOPE]. Our current relevant policies, controls and processes: [CURRENT_STATE]. Regulators and reporting lines: [REGULATORS].

Goal: Give compliance and the business a clear picture of what this change requires of us, where we fall short today, and the plan to be compliant by the deadline.

Task: Produce: (1) a plain-English summary of what is changing and the key new/changed obligations with references and dates; (2) an applicability assessment - which parts of our business, products or entities are in scope and which are not, with reasoning; (3) a gap analysis against our current state; (4) required actions (policy, process, system, training, disclosure, reporting) with owner, effort and due date working back from the deadline; (5) key risks and decisions for leadership.

Constraints: Base obligations only on the provided text; flag where interpretation or external counsel input is needed. Do not assert a compliance conclusion - present the gap and the required action. Be explicit about transition periods and any grandfathering.

Examples: Gap row: 'Obligation: [X] by [date]. Current state: [Y]. Gap: [Z]. Action: [action], owner [role], due [date], depends on [dependency].'

Format: Sections: What is changing | Applicability | Gap analysis (table) | Action plan (table) | Risks & decisions. ~700 words.

Verification: Check every obligation and date against the provided text; list points that require regulator guidance or external counsel to interpret.

Validation: Have compliance and, where flagged, external counsel confirm the interpretation before the action plan is committed. Pressure-test the timeline: is it achievable before the effective date? Escalate if not.

title: Build a compliance checklist and control map
description: Maps obligations to controls, gaps, owners, and remediation.
prompt:
Role: Act as a compliance officer building a compliance checklist and control map.

Context: Regulation / standard / internal policy in scope: [SOURCE]. Provided text or requirement list: [REQUIREMENTS]. Our processes and existing controls: [EXISTING_CONTROLS]. Business units affected: [BUSINESS_UNITS]. How compliance is currently evidenced and monitored: [CURRENT_MONITORING].

Task: Produce: a requirement-by-requirement checklist (requirement, reference, what 'done' looks like); the control(s) that address each (existing or 'gap - control needed'); the evidence that demonstrates it; the owner; and a suggested test/attestation frequency. Summarise the top gaps.

Format: A table: Requirement | Reference | Done looks like | Control | Evidence | Owner | Test frequency. Plus a gaps summary.

Verification: Tie every requirement to the provided source text; mark requirements with no current control clearly as gaps rather than assuming coverage.

Validation: Walk the checklist with a process owner from one business unit: can they actually produce the evidence listed? Adjust anything that is not practically evidenceable.

title: Draft a data protection impact assessment (DPIA)
description: A DPIA draft for a new system or process handling personal data.
prompt:
Role: Act as a data protection officer drafting a DPIA for review.

Context: Processing activity and its purpose: [ACTIVITY_PURPOSE]. Data categories, subjects and volumes (including any special-category data): [DATA_SUBJECTS]. Data flows, systems, recipients and any transfers: [FLOWS]. Legal basis relied on: [LEGAL_BASIS]. Retention: [RETENTION]. Stakeholders consulted: [CONSULTED]. Applicable framework: [FRAMEWORK] (e.g. UK GDPR).

Goal: Produce a DPIA draft that a DPO and legal can finalise: a clear description, a real necessity/proportionality analysis, and risks with mitigations that reduce them to an acceptable level.

Task: Draft: (1) a systematic description of the processing and the data flows; (2) the necessity and proportionality assessment against the purpose and legal basis, including whether a less intrusive option exists; (3) a risk assessment to data subjects (each risk: source, likelihood, severity, overall) covering unauthorised access, excessive collection, loss of control, re-identification, function creep, transfers; (4) mitigations per risk and the residual risk; (5) the consultation record and the sign-off / residual-risk decisions needed.

Constraints: This is a draft for the DPO and legal to complete and approve - not a final assessment and not legal advice. Do not assert that the legal basis is valid - present the analysis. Do not minimise special-category or vulnerable-subject risks. Flag any transfer needing a transfer mechanism.

Examples: Risk row: 'Risk: re-identification of pseudonymised records via [dataset]. Source: linkage. Likelihood: medium. Severity: high. Mitigation: [k-anonymity / access controls / DPA clause]. Residual: low-medium.'

Format: Sections: Processing description & flows | Necessity & proportionality | Risk assessment (table) | Mitigations & residual risk | Consultation & sign-offs needed. ~800 words.

Verification: Check every data category, flow and recipient in the description also appears in the risk assessment; flag missing legal-basis or transfer analysis.

Validation: The DPO and legal must review and approve before processing proceeds. Pressure-test the necessity analysis: would a regulator accept that a less intrusive alternative was truly considered? Strengthen if not.

title: Update a privacy notice and records of processing
description: Aligns your privacy notice and processing records with what you actually do with data.
prompt:
Role: Act as a data protection officer drafting a privacy notice section and RoPA entry.

Context: Processing activity: [ACTIVITY]. Data collected, from whom, and why: [DATA_PURPOSE]. Legal basis: [LEGAL_BASIS]. Recipients and any transfers: [RECIPIENTS_TRANSFERS]. Retention period and rationale: [RETENTION]. Data subject rights and how to exercise them: [RIGHTS]. Framework: [FRAMEWORK].

Task: Produce: (1) a privacy notice section in plain language - what we collect, why, the legal basis, who we share it with, transfers and safeguards, how long we keep it, the individual's rights and how to exercise them, and how to complain; (2) the matching record-of-processing entry in the standard fields.

Format: Two blocks: Privacy notice section (plain language) | RoPA entry (fielded).

Verification: Ensure the notice and the RoPA entry are consistent on purpose, legal basis, recipients, transfers and retention; flag any field where information is missing.

Validation: Read the notice as a non-expert data subject: is it genuinely understandable, or full of legalese? Simplify. The DPO should confirm the legal basis and transfer wording.

title: Review documents for due diligence red flags
description: A due diligence document review with red flags and follow-up questions.
prompt:
Role: Act as legal counsel conducting legal due diligence on a target for a transaction.

Context: Transaction type and rationale: [TRANSACTION]. Area(s) of DD in scope (e.g. material contracts, litigation, IP, employment, compliance): [DD_SCOPE]. Documents provided (index): [DOC_INDEX]. Deal issues that especially matter: [KEY_CONCERNS]. Materiality threshold: [MATERIALITY]. Governing law: [LAW].

Goal: Give the deal team a clear view of the legal red flags in the reviewed documents, ranked by how much they should affect the deal, and the follow-ups needed.
