title: Turn a rough video idea into a detailed video prompt
description: Paste a one-line video idea and get back a detailed, shot-by-shot prompt you can use in Veo, Sora, Kling or Gemini.
prompt:
Act as an experienced video director and prompt writer for AI video tools.

**My idea:** [ONE OR TWO SENTENCES, e.g. a cat waking up its owner on a rainy Monday]
**Tool I will use:** [Veo / Sora / Kling / Gemini / other]
**Length:** [5 / 8 / 10 seconds]
**Aspect ratio:** [16:9 / 9:16]
**Mood:** [funny / calm / dramatic / inspiring]

Task: Rewrite my idea as one detailed video prompt. Describe, in this order: subject (with consistent visual details), action from start to finish, setting and time of day, camera shot and movement, lens and visual style, lighting, and sound.

Format:
1. The finished prompt as one paragraph I can paste directly.
2. Two alternative versions: one with a different camera approach, one with a different mood.
3. Three short tips for fixing common problems if the first result isn't right.

Rules: keep it to one continuous shot unless I ask for cuts; no real, identifiable people, copyrighted characters, logos or on-screen text.

title: Turn my job duties into achievement-focused resume bullets
description: Rewrites duty-style resume lines into concise achievement bullets with results, and flags where you need to add a real number.
prompt:
Act as an experienced resume writer.

**Target role:** [JOB TITLE]
**My current bullets or duties:** [PASTE]
**Results I remember (even rough):** [e.g. cut response time, trained 5 people, grew sales]

Task: Rewrite each duty as an achievement bullet.

1. Use the pattern: strong action verb + what I did + the result or scale.
2. Keep each bullet to one or two lines (under 25 words).
3. Lead with the bullets most relevant to the target role.
4. Where a result needs a number I haven't given, write [ADD METRIC] rather than guessing.
5. Show a before/after table, then the final list ready to paste.

Rules: never invent results, tools or responsibilities; keep the language plain and specific; avoid clichés such as "results-driven" and "team player".
variables: e.g. cut response time, trained 5 people, grew sales

title: Write a resume summary for my target role
description: Writes three short, specific resume summaries for a target role from your experience, without buzzwords or invented claims.
prompt:
Write a professional summary for the top of my resume.

**Target role and level:** [e.g. senior data analyst]
**Years of experience and field:** [DETAILS]
**My strongest 2–3 achievements:** [ACHIEVEMENTS]
**Key skills the job asks for:** [PASTE FROM JOB DESCRIPTION]
**Industry or company type I'm targeting:** [DETAILS]

Task: Write three versions (concise 2 lines, standard 3–4 lines, and one that leads with a headline-style title).

Each version must:
- Say who I am professionally and what I'm best at, in the first sentence.
- Include one concrete achievement or scale.
- Use two or three of the job's keywords where they truthfully describe me.
- Avoid first-person pronouns and empty adjectives.

Never add skills or achievements I haven't listed; use [ADD DETAIL] where something is missing.

title: Check my resume for applicant tracking systems (ATS)
description: Reviews your resume for ATS readability and keyword match against a job description, with a prioritised list of honest fixes.
prompt:
Act as a recruiter who knows how applicant tracking systems (ATS) parse resumes.

**Job description:** [PASTE]
**My resume (pasted as text):** [PASTE]

Task:
1. Formatting check: flag anything an ATS may read badly (tables, columns, text in headers or footers, graphics, unusual section names, dates in odd formats).
2. Keyword match: list the job's most important skills and terms, and mark each as present / phrased differently / missing.
3. Section check: contact details, summary, experience, education and skills are clearly labelled and in a standard order.
4. Give the 8 most valuable fixes, most important first, with the exact wording to change.

Format: a short table for the keyword match, then a numbered fix list.

Rules: only suggest keywords that truthfully describe my experience; never recommend hiding text or stuffing keywords.

title: Write my first resume with little work experience
description: Builds a one-page first resume for a student or graduate from education, projects, volunteering and part-time work.
prompt:
Help me write my first resume.

**Role or internship I'm applying for:** [ROLE]
**Education:** [DEGREE / SCHOOL / GRADES IF STRONG]
**Projects, coursework or competitions:** [DETAILS]
**Part-time jobs, volunteering, clubs or leadership:** [DETAILS]
**Skills (tools, languages, software):** [LIST]
**Location and contact details:** [DETAILS]

Task: Write a one-page resume in this order: contact details, a 2-line summary, education, projects, experience, skills.

1. Turn projects and activities into achievement bullets (what I did and what came of it).
2. Use the language of the role where it truthfully fits.
3. Keep it clean and ATS-friendly: no tables or columns.
4. After the resume, list three things I could add in the next month to make it stronger.

Never invent experience, grades or skills; use [ADD DETAIL] where something is missing.

title: Explain a career gap on my resume and in interviews
description: Helps you present a career gap honestly and confidently on a resume, in a cover letter line and as a short interview answer.
prompt:
Help me address a gap in my career.

**Length and dates of the gap:** [e.g. March 2024 – June 2025]
**Reason (share only what you're comfortable with):** [caring for family / health / relocation / layoff / study / travel]
**What I did during it, if anything:** [courses, freelance, volunteering, projects]
**Role I'm applying for now:** [ROLE]

Task:
1. Suggest how to show the gap on my resume (a short line in the experience section or none), with exact wording.
2. Write one sentence I could use in a cover letter.
3. Write a 30-second interview answer that is honest, brief and moves quickly to why I'm ready for this role.
4. List two follow-up questions an interviewer might ask, with short answers.

Rules: keep it truthful and private where I want it private; never suggest hiding dates or inventing work.

title: Translate my experience from another field into resume language
description: Rewrites experience from another industry, the military or teaching into terms a new type of employer understands and values.
prompt:
Act as a career-change coach.

**Where my experience comes from:** [e.g. military, teaching, hospitality, academia, a different industry]
**My current bullets or a description of my work:** [PASTE]
**The role and industry I'm moving into:** [TARGET]
**Job description for that role (optional):** [PASTE]

Task:
1. Identify my transferable skills and match each to what the target role needs.
2. Replace jargon, ranks and internal terms with plain language a civilian or new-industry recruiter will understand.
3. Rewrite my bullets as achievements with scale and results.
4. Suggest a new resume summary that explains the move in one line.

Format: a translation table (original term → plain-language equivalent), then the rewritten bullets.

Never overstate my experience or invent results; mark missing numbers as [ADD METRIC].

2. Remove or merge low-value lines (old roles, generic duties, repeated skills), and explain each cut in a few words.
3. Tighten wording so most bullets fit on one line.
4. Keep the strongest achievements and any numbers.
5. Output the final one-page version, then a short list of what was removed so I can put anything back.

Rules: don't change facts, dates or job titles; don't add anything new.

Structure:

2. Paragraph linking two transferable strengths to the role's main requirements, with evidence.
3. Paragraph showing commitment to the new field (preparation, projects, learning).
4. Close with confidence and a clear next step.

Rules: under 350 words; no apologising for the change; never invent achievements or details about the company; use [ADD DETAIL] where something is missing.

title: Build the market analysis for my business plan

title: Build a three-year financial projection for my business plan

title: Write the marketing and sales section of my business plan

3. For each, say what evidence would satisfy you.
4. Point out the weakest assumption in the financials and how to test it.
5. Give a verdict: what would make you say yes, and what is a deal-breaker today.

Be direct and specific. Base everything on the plan; don't invent facts about my business.

title: Write a business plan for a local small business
description: Writes a practical business plan for a café, salon, shop or local service, focused on location, costs and getting customers.
prompt:
Act as a small-business adviser.

**Type of business:** [café / salon / retail shop / gym / repair service / other]
**Location and why there:** [DETAILS]
**Opening costs and funding:** [NUMBERS]
**Expected prices and customers per day:** [ESTIMATES]
**Staff plan:** [DETAILS]
**What makes it different from nearby competitors:** [DETAILS]

Task: Write a practical business plan with:
1. Concept and target customers.
2. Location analysis: foot traffic, nearby competitors, rent.
3. Daily operations and staffing.
4. Simple monthly profit and loss and the break-even number of customers per day (show the calculation).
5. Local marketing plan for the first three months.
6. Licences and permits to check locally.
7. Top risks and a plan B for each.

Rules: mark guesses [ASSUMPTION]; check legal requirements with local authorities.
variables: café / salon / retail shop / gym / repair service / other

title: Write a business plan for a nonprofit or social enterprise
description: Writes a plan for a nonprofit or social enterprise that connects impact, funding sources and sustainability for funders.
prompt:
Write a business plan for a nonprofit or social enterprise.

**Mission and the problem we address:** [DETAILS]
**Who we serve and how many:** [DETAILS]
**Programmes or products:** [DETAILS]
**Funding sources (current and planned):** [grants, donations, earned income, contracts]
**Team and partners:** [DETAILS]

Task:
1. Mission, problem and theory of change (inputs → activities → outputs → outcomes).
2. Programmes and how they are delivered.
3. Impact measurement: 3–5 indicators and how we'll collect them.
4. Funding model with a 3-year budget and the share from each source.
5. Sustainability: how we reduce dependence on any single funder.
6. Governance and risks.

Rules: no invented statistics or outcomes; mark gaps [ADD DATA]; keep the language plain for funders.

title: Write an elevator pitch from my business plan
description: Distils your business plan into 30-second, 60-second and one-line pitches for investors, customers and networking.
prompt:
Turn my business plan into elevator pitches.

**Business plan or summary:** [PASTE]
**Audiences:** [investors / customers / partners / networking events]

Task: Write:
1. A one-line description (under 15 words) a stranger would understand.
2. A 30-second pitch: problem, solution, why us, proof, ask.
3. A 60-second pitch that adds market, model and traction.
4. A version tailored to each audience I listed.
5. Three likely follow-up questions with short answers.

Rules: plain spoken language, no jargon; use only facts from the plan; mark missing proof as [ADD EVIDENCE].

title: Build a topic cluster and internal linking plan
description: Plans a pillar page and supporting articles around one topic, with keywords, search intent and an internal linking map.
prompt:
Act as an SEO content strategist.

**Core topic:** [TOPIC]
**My website and audience:** [URL, WHO IT SERVES]
**Existing pages on this topic:** [LIST URLS OR NONE]
**Keyword data (optional):** [PASTE]

Task:
1. Define one pillar page: target keyword, search intent and outline.
2. Propose 8–15 supporting articles, each with a primary keyword, intent (informational / commercial / transactional) and one-line angle.
3. Map internal links: every supporting article links to the pillar and to 1–2 related articles, with suggested anchor text.
4. Mark which existing pages to update, merge or redirect.
5. Order the plan by expected impact and effort.

Format: a table for the cluster, then the link map.

Rules: don't invent search volumes; label anything without data as [CHECK VOLUME].

title: Optimize my content for AI search and AI Overviews
description: Reviews a page for generative search (Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Perplexity) and rewrites it to be clearer and more quotable.
prompt:
Act as a generative engine optimisation (GEO) specialist.

**Page URL or content:** [PASTE]
**Questions people ask that this page should answer:** [LIST]
**Our expertise or first-hand evidence:** [DETAILS]

Task:
1. Check whether the page answers each question directly, in the first 1–2 sentences under a clear heading.
2. Rewrite the opening paragraph as a self-contained 40–60 word answer.
3. Turn headings into the questions people actually ask.
4. Add specific facts, definitions, comparisons or steps that are easy to quote, and mark where a source or data point is needed.
5. Suggest structured data (FAQPage, HowTo, Article) that fits the page.
6. List signals of expertise to add (author, date, first-hand experience).

Rules: keep the content accurate; never invent statistics or sources, use [ADD SOURCE].

title: Create a local SEO plan for my business
description: Builds a local SEO plan: Google Business Profile, location pages, reviews and local citations, prioritised for a small business.
prompt:
Act as a local SEO consultant.

**Business, category and services:** [DETAILS]
**Locations or service areas:** [CITIES / AREAS]
**Website:** [URL]
**Current Google Business Profile status:** [none / basic / complete]
**Main local competitors:** [NAMES]

Task: Create a 90-day local SEO plan with:
1. Google Business Profile: categories, services, description, photos, posts and Q&A to add.
2. Website: what each location or service-area page needs (unique content, NAP details, map, local proof).
3. Reviews: a simple, policy-compliant process to ask for reviews and reply to them.
4. Citations: the directories that matter for my category and country.
5. Local content ideas and local link opportunities.
6. What to track monthly.

Rules: no fake reviews, keyword-stuffed business names or fake addresses.

title: Write alt text for my website images
description: Writes concise, accessible alt text for a list of images that describes them for screen readers and helps image search.
prompt:
Write alt text for the images on my page.

**Page topic and purpose:** [DETAILS]
**Images (describe each, or upload them):** [1. … 2. … 3. …]
**Image role:** [informative / decorative / functional, e.g. a button or link]

Task: For each image:
1. Write alt text under 125 characters that describes what matters in this context.
2. If the image is purely decorative, say alt="" and why.
3. If the image contains text, include that text.
4. Use a relevant keyword only where it naturally describes the image.
5. Suggest a descriptive file name.

Format: a table with image, alt text, file name.

Rules: describe, don't sell; no "image of" or "picture of"; never keyword-stuff.
variables: informative / decorative / functional, e.g. a button or link

title: Plan a link-building outreach campaign
description: Plans an ethical link-building campaign: linkable assets, target sites, personalised outreach emails and follow-ups.
prompt:
Act as a digital PR and link-building specialist.

**My website and niche:** [URL, TOPIC]
**Pages I want links to:** [URLS]
**Assets I have or could create:** [original data, tools, guides, templates, expert quotes]
**Budget and time per week:** [DETAILS]

Task:
1. Recommend the 2–3 most linkable assets to create or improve, and why people would cite them.
2. Define target site types (resource pages, journalists, bloggers, partners, industry associations) and how to find them.
3. Write a personalised outreach email template under 120 words, plus a follow-up.
4. Plan a 6-week campaign with weekly targets.
5. Define what to measure.

Rules: no paid links, link schemes or private blog networks; emails must be honest and easy to say no to.
variables: original data, tools, guides, templates, expert quotes

title: Refresh an outdated blog post to win back rankings
description: Audits an older article that has lost traffic and plans an update: new information, search intent, structure and internal links.
prompt:
Act as an SEO editor.

**Article (paste text or URL content):** [PASTE]
**Target keyword:** [KEYWORD]
**What has changed since it was written:** [new facts, products, prices, laws]
**What currently ranks above it (optional):** [NOTES]

Task:
1. Check whether the article still matches the search intent; say what to change if not.
2. List outdated facts, broken examples and missing subtopics.
3. Propose a new outline with H2/H3 headings as questions where useful.
4. Rewrite the title tag, meta description and introduction.
5. Suggest internal links to and from the article.
6. Say whether to keep the URL (usually yes) and how to show it was updated.

Rules: flag anything that needs a current source as [VERIFY]; don't invent data.

title: Map search intent for a list of keywords
description: Classifies a keyword list by search intent and funnel stage and recommends the page type that should target each one.
prompt:
Act as an SEO strategist.

**My business and offer:** [DETAILS]
**Keyword list (with volumes if you have them):** [PASTE]

Task:
1. Classify each keyword: informational, commercial investigation, transactional or navigational.
2. Assign a funnel stage (awareness, consideration, decision).
3. Recommend the best page type for each (guide, comparison, product or category page, tool, landing page) and whether an existing page should target it.
4. Group keywords that one page can cover together.
5. Flag keywords that don't fit my business and should be dropped.

Format: a table, then a short list of the top 5 pages to create first.

Rules: don't invent volumes or difficulty; where intent is unclear, say to check the live search results.

title: Write SEO copy for an online store category page
description: Writes helpful category page copy for an online store, with an intro, buying guidance and FAQs that support rankings without stuffing.
prompt:
Write category page copy for my online store.

**Category:** [e.g. running shoes for women]
**Products in it:** [types, price range, brands]
**Target keyword and related terms:** [KEYWORDS]
**What shoppers usually need to decide:** [size, use case, material, budget]
**Brand voice:** [DESCRIBE]

Task:
1. A short intro (50–80 words) shown above the products.
2. A buying guide (200–300 words) shown below the products, with 2–3 subheadings.
3. Four FAQs with short answers.
4. A title tag (under 60 characters) and meta description (under 155).
5. Suggested links to related categories and guides.

Rules: helpful first, keywords only where natural; no claims I can't support ("best", "cheapest") unless I give proof.

title: Diagnose a sudden drop in organic traffic
description: Works through a structured diagnosis of a drop in Google traffic: tracking, technical issues, algorithm updates and content.
prompt:
Act as a technical SEO consultant diagnosing a traffic drop.

**When the drop started and how big:** [DATES, %]
**Which pages or sections fell:** [DETAILS FROM ANALYTICS / SEARCH CONSOLE]
**Recent changes to the site:** [redesign, migration, new CMS, content changes, robots.txt edits]
**Search Console notes:** [coverage errors, manual actions, indexing changes]

Task:
1. Rule out tracking problems first (analytics tag, consent changes, filters).
2. Check technical causes: noindex, robots.txt, canonicals, redirects, server errors, site speed.
3. Compare dates with known search algorithm updates; I will confirm the dates.
4. Check whether rankings, click-through rate or demand changed (seasonality).
5. Give a ranked list of likely causes, the evidence that would confirm each, and the fix.

Rules: don't claim a cause without evidence; list the exact reports to check.
variables: coverage errors, manual actions, indexing changes

title: Write JSON-LD schema markup for a page
description: Writes valid JSON-LD structured data for a page type such as Article, Product, LocalBusiness or FAQPage, using only real page content.
prompt:
Act as a structured data specialist.

**Page type:** [Article / Product / LocalBusiness / Organization / FAQPage / Event / Recipe / HowTo]
**Page URL:** [URL]
**Content to describe (paste the visible page content):** [PASTE]
**Business or publisher details:** [NAME, LOGO URL, SOCIAL PROFILES]

Task:
1. Write JSON-LD for the page using schema.org types and the properties search engines support for it.
2. Use only information that appears on the page; leave out anything I haven't given.
3. Add BreadcrumbList if the page has a breadcrumb trail.
4. List required versus recommended properties, and which ones are missing.
5. Tell me how to test it (Rich Results Test, Schema Markup Validator).

Rules: never mark up content that isn't visible on the page; no fake reviews or ratings.

title: Plan URLs and redirects for a website migration
description: Plans a site migration or redesign so rankings survive: URL mapping, redirects, launch checklist and post-launch monitoring.
prompt:
Act as a technical SEO lead planning a website migration.

**Type of migration:** [new domain / new CMS / redesign / HTTP to HTTPS / merging sites]
**Current site size and key sections:** [DETAILS]
**List of current URLs (or a sample):** [PASTE]
**New URL structure (if known):** [DETAILS]
**Launch date:** [DATE]

Task:
1. Rules for the new URL structure (short, lowercase, hyphenated, stable).
2. A redirect mapping approach: one-to-one 301s to the closest equivalent, never all to the home page.
3. A pre-launch checklist: crawl, benchmark rankings and traffic, staging blocked from indexing.
4. A launch-day checklist: redirects live, robots.txt, sitemaps, canonicals, analytics.
5. Post-launch monitoring for 8 weeks: what to check and when.

Format: checklists I can copy into a project tool.

title: Write product descriptions for a whole catalogue in one style
description: Writes consistent product descriptions for many products at once from a spreadsheet of attributes, in your brand voice.
prompt:
Act as an e-commerce copywriter.

**Brand voice:** [e.g. warm and practical / premium and minimal / playful]
**Target customer:** [WHO]
**Product data (paste rows: name, category, materials, sizes, features, price):** [PASTE]
**Length per description:** [e.g. 60–90 words + 3 bullets]

Task:
1. Define a short template first: opening line, benefit paragraph, 3 feature bullets, care or spec line.
2. Write a description for each product following that template.
3. Vary the opening lines so the products don't sound copied from one another.
4. Output as a table (product name, description, bullets) I can paste into a spreadsheet.

Rules: use only attributes in the data, and write [MISSING: attribute] where something important is absent; no claims about health, safety or results I haven't provided.
variables: e.g. warm and practical / premium and minimal / playful

title: Write a Shopify product page that sells and ranks
description: Writes every field of an online store product page: title, description, bullets, SEO title, meta description and image alt text.
prompt:
Write the full product page for my online store.

**Product:** [NAME]
**Key features and specs:** [LIST]
**Who it's for and the problem it solves:** [DETAILS]
**Price and what's included:** [DETAILS]
**Shipping, returns and guarantee:** [DETAILS]
**Target keyword:** [KEYWORD]
**Brand voice:** [DESCRIBE]

Task: Write:
1. Product title (clear, under 70 characters).
2. Description: a benefit-led opening, a short paragraph on use, and 4–6 feature bullets.
3. A "What's in the box" or specs section.
4. SEO title (under 60 characters) and meta description (under 155).
5. Alt text for up to 5 product images I describe: [IMAGES].
6. Two short FAQs.

Rules: no invented specs, awards or reviews; mark gaps [ADD DETAIL].

title: Write an Etsy listing title, tags and description
description: Writes an Etsy listing with a searchable title, 13 relevant tags and a warm description that answers buyers' questions.
prompt:
Act as an Etsy shop consultant.

**Item:** [WHAT IT IS]
**Materials, size, colours and variations:** [DETAILS]
**Handmade, vintage or supplies:** [TYPE]
**Who buys it and for what occasion:** [e.g. gift for new mums, wedding decor]
**Processing time, shipping and personalisation options:** [DETAILS]

Task:
1. A title that puts the clearest search phrase first and reads naturally (no keyword lists).
2. Exactly 13 tags, each up to 20 characters, using different phrases buyers would search.
3. A description: opening that describes the item and feeling, details (size, materials, care), personalisation steps, shipping and a short shop story line.
4. Suggested attributes and category to choose.

Rules: describe the item accurately; don't use other brands' trademarks in tags or title.
variables: e.g. gift for new mums, wedding decor

title: Turn a spec sheet into benefit-led product bullets
description: Converts technical specifications into clear benefit bullets that explain what each feature means for the buyer.
prompt:
Turn my product specifications into benefit-led bullet points.

**Product and category:** [DETAILS]
**Spec sheet:** [PASTE]
**Target buyer and what they care about most:** [DETAILS]
**Number of bullets:** [5 / 7]

Task:
1. For each important spec, write what it means for the buyer (feature → benefit).
2. Order the bullets by what the buyer cares about most.
3. Start each bullet with the benefit, then the supporting spec in a few words.
4. Keep each bullet under 25 words.
5. Add a feature → benefit table showing your reasoning, so I can check it.

Rules: every benefit must follow from a spec I gave; no exaggerated claims; keep units and numbers exactly as in the spec sheet.

title: Write a product description for a luxury or premium product
description: Writes an understated, premium product description focused on craft, materials and experience rather than hype.
prompt:
Act as a copywriter for premium brands.

**Product:** [NAME, CATEGORY]
**Materials, craft and origin:** [DETAILS]
**What makes it special:** [DESIGN STORY, MAKER, LIMITED EDITION…]
**Price point:** [PRICE]
**Brand voice references (describe):** [e.g. quiet confidence, heritage, modern minimal]

Task:
1. A short headline line (under 10 words).
2. A description of 80–120 words that leads with the experience of owning or using it, then the materials and craft.
3. Three detail lines (materials, dimensions, care).
4. A shorter version for social media.

Style: understated and precise; specific sensory detail; no exclamation marks, superlatives or discount language.

Rules: only facts I provide; mark gaps [ADD DETAIL].
variables: e.g. quiet confidence, heritage, modern minimal

title: Write a product description for a technical or B2B product
description: Writes a clear B2B product description that covers use cases, specifications, integrations and proof for business buyers.
prompt:
Write a product description for business buyers.

**Product:** [NAME, WHAT IT DOES]
**Buyer roles involved:** [e.g. operations manager, IT, finance]
**Main use cases and problems solved:** [LIST]
**Specifications, compatibility and integrations:** [DETAILS]
**Proof:** [certifications, customer results, case studies]
**Pricing model:** [DETAILS]

Task:
1. A one-sentence value statement.
2. A short overview paragraph for the decision-maker.
3. Use cases, each with the outcome for the business.
4. A specifications and compatibility table for technical evaluators.
5. A proof section using only the evidence I gave.
6. A call to action (demo, quote, datasheet).

Rules: precise language over hype; never invent certifications, figures or customers.

title: Rewrite supplier product copy in my brand voice
description: Rewrites manufacturer or supplier product text into original copy in your brand voice, so your pages aren't duplicates of other stores.
prompt:
Rewrite supplier product descriptions so they are original and match my brand.

**Supplier or manufacturer text:** [PASTE]
**My brand voice:** [DESCRIBE, with an example of copy I like]
**My customer:** [WHO]
**Anything I add that the supplier doesn't:** [warranty, bundle, fast shipping, local support]

Task:
1. Extract the facts from the supplier text (specs, materials, sizes, care).
2. Write a new description in my voice built around my customer's needs.
3. Add my store's own value (from above) where relevant.
4. Write a new title and 4–5 bullets.

Rules: keep every fact accurate; change structure and wording substantially so it isn't duplicate content; don't copy marketing claims I can't verify.
variables: DESCRIBE, with an example of copy I like
warranty, bundle, fast shipping, local support

title: Write a size, fit and care section that reduces returns
description: Writes clear size, fit and care guidance for a clothing or home product page to help buyers choose right first time.
prompt:
Write the size, fit and care section for my product page.

**Product:** [NAME, TYPE]
**Size chart or measurements:** [PASTE]
**How it fits compared with standard sizes:** [runs small / true to size / relaxed]
**Fabric or materials and stretch:** [DETAILS]
**Model or reference measurements (optional):** [DETAILS]
**Common reasons for returns:** [DETAILS]

Task:
1. A short fit summary in plain words ("Relaxed fit; if you're between sizes, size down").
2. A clean size table using my measurements.
3. How to measure yourself, in 3 steps.
4. Care instructions.
5. Two FAQs that address the common return reasons.

Rules: use only my measurements and facts; never guess sizes.
variables: runs small / true to size / relaxed

title: Write product FAQs from customer reviews and questions
description: Turns real customer reviews and questions into a short product FAQ that answers objections before people buy.
prompt:
Create a product FAQ from what customers actually say.

**Product:** [NAME]
**Customer reviews, questions and support messages:** [PASTE]
**Product facts and policies:** [SPECS, SHIPPING, RETURNS, WARRANTY]

Task:
1. Group the questions and concerns into themes and count how often each appears.
2. Write 6–8 FAQs for the most common themes, with short, honest answers based on the product facts.
3. Note any recurring complaint that the FAQ can't fix and should go to the product team.
4. Suggest which answers to move into the main product description.

Rules: answer only from the facts I gave; don't promise anything not in my policies; don't quote customers by name.

title: Write a product launch email for a new product
description: Writes a launch email for a new product with subject lines, a clear benefit, proof and one call to action.
prompt:
Write an email announcing a new product.

**Product and launch date:** [DETAILS]
**Who the list is:** [customers / subscribers / segment]
**The main benefit and who it's for:** [DETAILS]
**Launch offer (if any) and deadline:** [DETAILS]
**Proof or early feedback:** [DETAILS]
**Link:** [URL]

Task:
1. Five subject lines and preview texts (different angles: benefit, curiosity, news, offer, problem).
2. The email: a short hook, what the product is, the main benefit, 3 short points, proof, one clear call to action.
3. A short reminder email for the day before the offer ends.

Rules: under 200 words per email; one call to action; no false urgency or claims I haven't given.

title: Write product descriptions for food and drink products
description: Writes appetising food and beverage product descriptions with ingredients, allergens and serving ideas, avoiding unproven health claims.
prompt:
Act as a food and beverage copywriter.

**Product:** [NAME, TYPE]
**Ingredients and allergens:** [LIST]
**Taste, texture and aroma notes:** [DETAILS]
**Origin, producer or method:** [DETAILS]
**Size, shelf life and storage:** [DETAILS]
**Serving ideas:** [DETAILS]

Task:
1. A sensory description of 60–100 words.
2. A serving or pairing suggestions line.
3. An ingredients and allergens block, written clearly.
4. Storage and shelf-life details.
5. A one-line version for marketplaces.

Rules: no health or nutrition claims ("boosts immunity", "healthy") unless I provide approved wording; show allergens prominently; follow my country's labelling rules, which I will confirm.

title: Create a product comparison table for my store
description: Builds a clear comparison of similar products in your store so shoppers can choose the right one and buy with confidence.
prompt:
Create a comparison to help shoppers choose between my products.

**Products to compare:** [NAMES]
**Specs and prices for each:** [PASTE]
**Who each product is best for (my view):** [NOTES]

Task:
1. A comparison table with the 6–8 attributes that matter most for the decision.
2. A "Best for" line under each product.
3. A short "How to choose" guide (3–4 questions that point to the right product).
4. A one-paragraph intro for the comparison page or section.

Rules: compare only on facts I provided; be honest about trade-offs; no claims about competitors' products.

title: Turn a rough idea into a detailed AI image prompt
description: Turns a one-line picture idea into a detailed image prompt with subject, style, lighting and composition, plus versions for different tools.
prompt:
Act as an expert prompt writer for AI image generators.

**My idea:** [ONE OR TWO SENTENCES]
**Tool I'll use:** [Midjourney / ChatGPT (DALL·E) / Gemini / Flux / Stable Diffusion / other]
**Where the image will be used:** [website hero / social post / slide / print / just for fun]
**Aspect ratio:** [16:9 / 1:1 / 4:5 / 9:16]

Task: Write one detailed image prompt that describes, in this order:
1. Subject and action, with specific visual details.
2. Setting and background.
3. Style or medium (photo, illustration, 3D render, watercolour…).
4. Lighting and colour palette.
5. Composition and camera angle.
6. Mood.

Then give: a short version for tools that prefer brief prompts, two variations with a different style, and a list of things to avoid (for example extra fingers, text, clutter).

Rules: no real people, named living artists, brands or copyrighted characters.
variables: website hero / social post / slide / print / just for fun

title: Create a product photo prompt on a clean studio background
description: A text-to-image template for a clean e-commerce product shot on a plain background with soft studio light.
prompt:
Create a professional studio product photograph.

**Product:** [describe the product: shape, colour, material, size]
**Background:** [pure white / soft grey gradient / pastel colour: COLOUR]
**Angle:** [front / three-quarter view / top-down flat lay]
**Props (optional):** [none / a few simple props that suit the product]
**Aspect ratio:** [1:1 for marketplaces / 4:5 / 16:9]

Style: high-end commercial product photography, soft diffused studio lighting, gentle realistic shadow under the product, sharp focus across the whole product, true-to-life colours, crisp edges, lots of clean space around the product.

Avoid: text, logos, watermarks, reflections that hide the product, distorted shapes, extra objects.

Note: an AI image is a concept or mock-up; use real photos of your actual product for listings so buyers see exactly what they get.
variables: describe the product: shape, colour, material, size
pure white / soft grey gradient / pastel colour: COLOUR
front / three-quarter view / top-down flat lay
none / a few simple props that suit the product

title: Create a lifestyle product scene prompt
description: A prompt for an AI lifestyle image that shows a product being used in a realistic setting, for ads and social posts.
prompt:
Create a lifestyle photograph showing a product in use.

**Product:** [describe it]
**Setting:** [cosy kitchen in morning light / modern office desk / outdoor café / bathroom shelf / hiking trail]
**Who is using it (optional):** [no people / hands only / a person described generally, e.g. a woman in her 30s, seen from behind]
**Mood:** [calm / energetic / premium / homely]
**Colour palette:** [warm neutrals / bright and fresh / brand colours: COLOURS]
**Aspect ratio:** [4:5 / 1:1 / 9:16 / 16:9]

Style: natural editorial photography, soft natural light, shallow depth of field with the product in sharp focus, realistic textures, uncluttered composition with space for text on one side.

Avoid: text, logos, distorted hands, extra fingers, identifiable real people.
variables: warm neutrals / bright and fresh / brand colours: COLOURS

title: Generate logo concept ideas with AI
description: A prompt for exploring simple logo concepts with an AI image tool, as inspiration for a designer to refine into a real logo.
prompt:
Create a sheet of 6 simple logo concepts.

**Brand name:** [NAME]
**What the business does:** [ONE LINE]
**Personality:** [e.g. trustworthy, playful, premium, eco-friendly, technical]
**Symbol ideas (optional):** [e.g. a leaf, a bridge, an abstract mark]
**Colours:** [up to 2–3 colours, or black only]

Style: flat vector logo marks, simple geometric shapes, strong silhouette that works small and in one colour, centred on a plain white background, each concept in its own square, evenly spaced grid.

Avoid: gradients, photorealism, tiny details, mock-ups, resemblance to existing well-known logos.

Note: AI image tools often misspell text, so ask for symbols only and add the brand name in design software. Use these as concepts for a designer, and check trademarks before using any logo.
variables: e.g. trustworthy, playful, premium, eco-friendly, technical
e.g. a leaf, a bridge, an abstract mark
up to 2–3 colours, or black only

title: Create a flat vector illustration prompt for a website
description: A prompt for clean flat vector illustrations for websites, blog headers and presentations, in a consistent style.
prompt:
Create a flat vector illustration.

**Scene or concept:** [e.g. a small team planning around a whiteboard / a person working remotely from a balcony / data flowing between devices]
**Use:** [website hero / blog header / slide / empty-state graphic]
**Colour palette:** [3–5 colours: COLOURS, or a calm blue and coral palette]
**Background:** [plain / soft shapes / white]
**Aspect ratio:** [16:9 / 4:3 / 1:1]

Style: modern flat vector illustration, simple geometric shapes, consistent line weight, limited colour palette, friendly people with simplified faces, generous negative space, clean edges suitable for the web.

Avoid: text, logos, photorealism, clutter, gradients unless I ask for them.

Tip: to keep a set consistent, reuse the same style sentence and palette for every illustration.
variables: website hero / blog header / slide / empty-state graphic

title: Create a watercolour illustration prompt
description: A prompt for soft watercolour-style illustrations for cards, prints, book covers and social posts.
prompt:
Create a watercolour illustration.

**Subject:** [e.g. a quiet harbour at dawn / a bouquet of wildflowers in a jar / a fox in a snowy forest]
**Colour palette:** [soft pastels / muted earth tones / vibrant: COLOURS]
**Composition:** [centred subject with white space / full scene / vignette that fades to white edges]
**Use:** [greeting card / wall print / book cover / social post]
**Aspect ratio:** [5:7 / 1:1 / 4:5]

Style: traditional watercolour on textured cold-press paper, soft wet-on-wet blends, visible pigment granulation, delicate pencil underdrawing, gentle light, hand-painted feel.

Avoid: text, digital-looking hard edges, oversaturation, imitation of any named living artist.
variables: soft pastels / muted earth tones / vibrant: COLOURS
greeting card / wall print / book cover / social post

title: Create a 3D isometric icon or scene prompt
description: A prompt for clean 3D isometric icons and mini-scenes for apps, websites and presentations.
prompt:
Create a 3D isometric illustration.

**Object or scene:** [e.g. a tiny office with a desk and plants / a shield with a lock for security / a shopping cart with parcels]
**Use:** [app icon / feature icon set / landing page / slide]
**Colour palette:** [soft pastel / brand colours: COLOURS]
**Background:** [plain white / soft gradient / transparent-looking light grey]
**Aspect ratio:** [1:1 / 4:3]

Style: clean 3D isometric render, soft rounded shapes, matte clay-like materials, soft studio lighting with gentle shadows, minimal detail, centred composition with space around it.

Avoid: text, logos, clutter, photorealistic textures.

Tip: for an icon set, keep the same lighting, angle and palette sentence for every icon and change only the object.
variables: app icon / feature icon set / landing page / slide
plain white / soft gradient / transparent-looking light grey

title: Create a cinematic landscape or scene prompt
description: A prompt for dramatic, cinematic landscape and scene images for wallpapers, headers and storytelling.
prompt:
Create a cinematic wide-angle image.

**Scene:** [e.g. a lone lighthouse on cliffs in a storm / a neon-lit city street after rain / misty mountains at sunrise / a desert road at dusk]
**Time and weather:** [golden hour / blue hour / fog / rain / clear night with stars]
**Mood:** [epic / peaceful / mysterious / hopeful]
**Aspect ratio:** [21:9 / 16:9 / 9:16 for phone wallpaper]

Style: cinematic photography, wide-angle lens, strong sense of depth with foreground, middle ground and background, dramatic natural lighting, rich but realistic colour grading, atmospheric haze, high detail.

Avoid: text, watermarks, people close to the camera, oversaturated colours.

Variation: add "shot on 35mm film, subtle grain" for a more analogue look.
variables: golden hour / blue hour / fog / rain / clear night with stars

title: Create a food photography prompt
description: A prompt for appetising food images for menus, recipe blogs and social posts, with styling and lighting control.
prompt:
Create a food photograph.

**Dish:** [describe the dish, ingredients and garnish]
**Plate and surface:** [rustic wooden board / white ceramic plate on linen / dark slate]
**Angle:** [overhead flat lay / 45-degree / close-up at table height]
**Props:** [cutlery, napkin, a few raw ingredients, a drink]
**Lighting:** [soft window light from the side / moody dark background with one light]
**Aspect ratio:** [4:5 / 1:1 / 16:9]

Style: professional editorial food photography, appetising and fresh, realistic textures, gentle steam if hot, shallow depth of field, natural colours.

Avoid: text, logos, plastic-looking food, extra cutlery or hands in odd positions.

Note: if you sell this dish, use a real photo in menus and listings so customers see what they'll get.
variables: describe the dish, ingredients and garnish
overhead flat lay / 45-degree / close-up at table height
cutlery, napkin, a few raw ingredients, a drink

title: Create an interior design visualisation prompt
description: A prompt for visualising a room design idea, style and colour scheme before you renovate or decorate.
prompt:
Create an interior design visualisation.

**Room:** [living room / bedroom / kitchen / home office / café interior]
**Size and shape:** [e.g. small square room with one large window]
**Style:** [Scandinavian / Japandi / industrial / mid-century modern / traditional Indian / coastal]
**Colour palette and materials:** [e.g. warm white walls, oak wood, linen, terracotta accents]
**Key furniture and features:** [LIST]
**Aspect ratio:** [16:9 / 4:3]

Style: photorealistic architectural interior photography, natural daylight from the window, wide-angle lens at eye level, straight vertical lines, realistic materials and proportions, styled but lived-in.

Avoid: text, distorted furniture, impossible structures, people.

Note: this is a mood visual; check real dimensions, materials and safety with a professional before building.
variables: living room / bedroom / kitchen / home office / café interior
e.g. small square room with one large window
e.g. warm white walls, oak wood, linen, terracotta accents

title: Create a children's book illustration prompt
description: A prompt for warm, consistent children's picture-book illustrations with a recurring character you describe.
prompt:
Create a children's picture-book illustration.

**Main character (keep identical in every image):** [e.g. a small round hedgehog with a red scarf and big curious eyes]
**Scene:** [what is happening on this page]
**Setting:** [e.g. a cosy village bakery in winter]
**Mood:** [cosy / adventurous / funny / calm bedtime]
**Aspect ratio:** [4:3 / 1:1 / two-page spread 2:1]

Style: warm hand-painted gouache look, soft rounded shapes, gentle textures, friendly expressions, rich but soft colours, simple background that leaves space for text at the [top / bottom].

Avoid: text in the image, scary or sharp features, copyrighted characters, imitation of any named living illustrator.

Tip: paste the same character description into every page's prompt, and upload a previous image as a reference if your tool allows it.
variables: what is happening on this page
e.g. a cosy village bakery in winter

title: Create a seamless pattern prompt for prints and backgrounds
description: A prompt for seamless, repeating patterns for fabric, wrapping paper, wallpapers and website backgrounds.
prompt:
Create a seamless repeating pattern.

**Motifs:** [e.g. lemons and leaves / geometric tiles / tiny stars and moons / paisley]
**Style:** [flat vector / watercolour / block print / line art]
**Colours:** [background COLOUR plus 2–4 motif colours]
**Density:** [sparse / medium / dense]
**Use:** [fabric / gift wrap / phone wallpaper / website background]

Style: seamless tileable pattern, edges that continue perfectly when repeated, evenly balanced motifs with no obvious grid, flat even lighting, high resolution, square format 1:1.

Avoid: text, logos, shadows or perspective, a single large central object.

Tip: test the tile by placing four copies side by side; if a seam shows, ask for the edges to be fixed.
variables: flat vector / watercolour / block print / line art
fabric / gift wrap / phone wallpaper / website background
